heading: Start here / What Towinly is (1)
text:
Towinly introduces older people to younger helpers, and then gives the friendship room to grow.

The app says it in its own words on the Guide screen: "Towinly is a community that brings older people and younger helpers together, so no one feels alone and everyday help is easy to find."

A friendship here climbs seven small steps, and both people have to agree to every one of them. You cannot buy your way up, and nobody can move a step on their own. That slowness is the design. As the app puts it: Help is easy to find. Trust takes time.

The Guide screen, inside the app under Profile.

Three kinds of account

When somebody joins, they choose one of three seats. What you see when you open the app depends on which one you picked.

Seat | Who it is for | What they do
Elder | Someone who would like company or a hand with everyday things | Ask for help, build friendships, check in daily, share stories
Helper | Someone who would like to help, often a student or a neighbour | Offer help on requests, build friendships, collect reviews
Family | The son, daughter or relative of an elder | Watch over a parent, see the friendships the parent shares, act for them if allowed

heading: Start here / What Towinly is (2)
text:
Note: A family member can never post a request or offer help. They watch, and they help their parent from the side, which is how Towinly is built.

The story it shows you first

The very first time Towinly is opened on a phone, it tells its own story across seven screens before asking anything of you. Swipe up to move through them, or tap Skip at the top. It runs once. After that the app opens on Log In instead.

Screen 1 of 7. The Trust Ladder, screen 5. Family, screen 6.

What this guide covers

Every screen you can reach in the app, in the order you meet it. Part one is for everybody. Part two is for elders, part three for helpers, part four for family. Part five goes back to the things all three share: trust, messages, your profile, safety and your data.

heading: Start here / Getting in (1)
text:
Three ways in: look around with a sample account, make your own, or sign in to one you already have.

The Log In screen. The three sample accounts sit at the bottom.

Look around first, with a sample account

You do not have to sign up to see how Towinly works. Three sample accounts are open to anyone, and they need no typing at all.

1. Open Towinly. The Log In screen appears.
2. Scroll to the bottom, under the line "Just want to see how it works? Look around with a sample account."
3. Tap Try as an Elder for Margaret, Try as a Helper for Harsha, or Try as Family for Sarah, who is Margaret's daughter.
4. The app opens on that person's own home screen. Every picture in this guide was taken this way.

Take care: The sample accounts are shared with everybody who downloads Towinly, and their contents reset by themselves. Please do not type anything private into one.

Making your own account

Signing up takes two screens and one email.

heading: Start here / Getting in (2)
text:
1. On the Log In screen, tap Create Account at the bottom.
2. Towinly asks "Who are you joining as?". Tap Elder, Helper, or I'm here for a family member. One tap moves you straight on, there is no Continue button.
3. Fill in the form: a username, your email, your date of birth, and a password of at least eight characters, typed twice. You have to be 18 or over to join.
4. Tick "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy". The Create Account button stays greyed out until you do, and the screen says why.
5. Tap Create Account. Towinly emails you a link.
6. Open the email and tap the link. Your account is made at that moment, and not before. Then come back to Towinly and sign in.

One tap picks your seat. Nothing is sent until you agree to the terms.

Tip: Cannot find the email? Look in your Spam or Junk folder. The app has a Resend email button on the screen it leaves you on.

A date of birth can be typed the way you would say it. Both "14 May 1953" and "1953-05-14" are understood. Only your age is ever shown to other people, never the date.

Signing in

heading: Start here / Getting in (3)
text:
1. Type your username, your Gmail address or your phone number into the first box. Any of the three works, which is why the box is labelled "Username, Gmail, or phone".
2. Type your password underneath.
3. Tap Log In.

Forgotten it? Tap Forgot password? and give your email address. Towinly sends a link for setting a new one. The screen says the same thing whether or not that email has an account, so nobody can use it to find out who is a member.

Signing out

Towinly asks before it logs you out. Nothing is deleted.

1. Tap Profile, the last button on the bar at the bottom.
2. Scroll to the very bottom of that screen. Log out is always the last thing on the page.
3. Tap it. Towinly asks "Log out?" and warns that you will need your username and password to get back in.
4. Tap Log out again to confirm, or Cancel to stay.

heading: Start here / Finding your way around (1)
text:
One bar at the bottom, one row at the top, and a helper you can ask at any time.

The bar at the bottom

Everything starts from the bar along the bottom of the screen. It has up to five places, and what sits in them depends on which kind of account you signed in with.

Your seat | First | Second | Middle | Fourth | Fifth
Elder | My Helpers | Posted Help | Ask Help | Messages | Profile
Helper | My Elders |  | Offer Help | Messages | Profile
Family | My Parents |  | none | Messages | Profile

The middle button is raised, round and sky blue. It is the one thing the app most wants you to be able to reach with your thumb. A family member has no middle button at all, because family never post or offer help.

The row at the top

Three things live above your home screen. On the left, a button that opens Add Friends, or Add parent if you are family. In the middle, the Towinly name. On the right, two small buttons: a shield with your trust score, which opens your Trust Score page, and a bell, which opens Updates. The bell carries a red number when something is waiting.

Ask AI

heading: Start here / Finding your way around (2)
text:
A small oval marked Ask AI floats above the bar at the bottom on every main screen. Tap it and a panel slides up where you can ask a question in plain words, by typing or by speaking. It can read its answers aloud. Three questions are offered to start you off: "What should I do today?", "How does the Trust Journey work?" and "What is my trust score?"

Ask AI opens as a panel over whatever you were doing.

Before your very first question, Towinly asks permission once. The answers are written by an outside service called OpenAI, and your question, that conversation and a short summary of your Towinly activity go to it. Your contact details never do. Tap Yes, that's okay to go ahead, or Not now to stop. Your typed question stays where it is either way.

Take care: Answers are written by a machine, so they can be wrong. Every answer has a flag button for reporting it, which carries the answer into the feedback form for you.

Refreshing a screen

Pull any main screen down with your finger and let go. Towinly fetches everything on it again. Use it if something looks out of date.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (1)
text:
One tap tells the people who love you that you are alright today.

Signing in as an elder takes you straight to your check-in. It is the only thing Towinly asks of you each day, and it takes one tap.

The check-in screen later on a day that is already done: the greeting and date, Your family knows you're alright today., the tick line Checked in for today, who can see it, the run of days, and the way out at the bottom.

1. Open Towinly. The check-in screen appears by itself, once a day.
2. Tap I'm here today.
3. The screen changes to "Your family knows you're alright today." and names who can see it.

Under the button, Towinly tells you exactly who will see it, by name: "Sarah, David and one other can see you checked in." If you have not linked any family yet, it shows a link that says Add your family instead.

Getting back to it later

Tap Profile, then Daily check-in. The screen is the same one.

The check-in belongs to the elder seat. If you joined Towinly as an Elder, you have a check-in screen. If you joined as a Helper or for a family member, you do not, and the rest of this chapter is not about your app.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (2)
text:
The top of the screen greets you by your first name. Before noon it says Good morning, until six in the evening Good afternoon, and after that Good evening. Under the greeting is today's date in words, written the way your own phone writes dates, in its language and its order.

Above the check-in sits a small card headed What's a check-in?. It says: One tap on I'm here today tells your trusted people you're okay. Skipping a day is fine. It's a gentle signal, never a duty. The card stays there on every visit until you tap Got it. After that tap it does not come back. The other button on it, Read the Guide, opens the short How Towinly works page inside the app, which is a much shorter thing than the guide you are holding.

The two states of the card

Before you check in, the big line reads Let your family know you're alright. and one blue button sits under it: I'm here today. While it is sending, the button reads Checking in… and cannot be tapped again, so a second tap by accident does nothing.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (3)
text:
Once it is done, the big line becomes Your family knows you're alright today. and the button is replaced by a green tick with words beside it. Straight after your tap the tick line reads Day 7 . See you tomorrow, with your own number in place of 7. If you come back to the screen later the same day, the tick line simply reads Checked in for today.

1. Open the check-in screen.
2. Tap I'm here today.
3. Wait while the button reads Checking in….
4. Read the green tick line that takes its place. It names the day you have reached.
5. Tap Take me home when you are ready to leave.

Who sees it, by name

A line under the button names the people this one tap reaches. The words change with how many there are, and with whether you have checked in yet.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (4)
text:
- One person linked: Sarah will see this. After you tap, the same line reads Sarah can see you checked in.
- Two people: Sarah and David will see this.
- Three people: Sarah, David and one other will see this. With four or more, the rest are counted, like Sarah, David and 2 others will see this.
- Nobody linked yet: a link that says Add your family, with the words and they will see you checked in. beside it. Tapping it opens the screen headed My Family.
- If Towinly cannot reach your family list at that moment, the whole line stays off the screen. It says nothing rather than telling you wrongly that nobody is linked.

Note: The check-in carries nothing else. It says you are here today, and that is all.

Your streak

Below the button and the names line, or below the green tick line once you have checked in, sits a large number with the words days in a row beside it, or day in a row when the number is 1. Under that are seven circles marked M T W T F S S. They run Monday to Sunday for the week you are in.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (5)
text:
What a circle shows | What it means
A green tick | A day inside your run of check-ins
A blue ring with a small dot, and a blue letter | Today, still waiting for your check-in
A plain grey circle | Any other day: one you missed, or one still to come this week

The number counts days that follow each other. Check in the day after your last one and it goes up by one. Leave a gap of a day or more and your next check-in starts the count again at 1. The seven circles are drawn from that same run, so a day you did check in before a break shows as a plain circle. Towinly keeps no day by day diary of your check-ins.

The three ways to reach this screen

Two of them bring the screen to you. Opening Towinly when you are already signed in as an elder takes you straight here, and so does logging in, whether today is checked in or not. And if you are on My Helpers with today's check-in still waiting, the app walks you here once.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (6)
text:
The way out is at the bottom, and its words change with the state. Before you check in it reads Not now, take me home. Once you have checked in it reads Take me home. Both go to My Helpers. Nothing moves you on by itself after you check in: the number stays on screen until you choose to leave.

Below the check-in card is one quiet row, Peekaboo, with the words A quiet minute with the tortoise and a Play button. It opens the Peekaboo game and has nothing to do with your check-in.

Tip: The Daily check-in row in Profile is also shown to helpers. A helper who taps it is sent straight back to their own home, because only elders have a check-in.

If the check-in does not go through

When your check-in cannot be loaded, the whole inside of the card is replaced by the words We couldn't load your check-in right now. Please check your connection and try again. and a Try again button. The big line, the I'm here today button, the names line and the number all go with it, so a weak connection never looks like a broken streak. You cannot check in until it loads. Tap Try again once your connection is back.

heading: If you are an elder / Your daily check-in (7)
text: If the tap itself fails, a short message appears saying Could not check in right now. Please try again. and the button goes back to I'm here today. Nothing is lost. Checking in twice in one day never counts twice.

heading: If you are an elder / My Helpers, your home screen (1)
text:
Everyone you are building a friendship with, and the step each friendship is on.

My Helpers. Two groups, and a row for each person.

The first button on the bar at the bottom is My Helpers. It holds a card for every helper you are connected to, sorted into two groups you can switch between: Building Trust for the friendships still climbing, and Trusted Friends for the ones that have reached the top.

Each row shows the helper's photo, or their initials if they have no photo, and their name. Tap a row to open it. Inside you see which of the seven steps the friendship is on, how many of the 15 trust points they have earned with you, and the buttons for moving it on.

Moving a friendship one step up

In Towinly the elder always starts a step and the helper accepts it. A helper can never move a friendship on by themselves.

heading: If you are an elder / My Helpers, your home screen (2)
text:
1. Tap the helper's card to open it.
2. Tap Start the next step.
3. Towinly asks "Start the next step?" and explains: "Trust grows only when BOTH of you agree. {Name} will get a tap to accept."
4. Tap Start to send it, or Not yet to leave things as they are.
5. The helper sees the request on their own phone. Once they accept, the step is climbed for both of you and Towinly says "You both agreed. One step up the ladder!"

Until they answer, the app tells you it is waiting for them. The Trust Ladder, in part five, lists all seven steps and what each one unlocks.

Pausing a friendship

At the bottom of an open card is Take a break. Towinly asks first, and explains that trust steps and messages pause until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost, and you can start again whenever you like.

The buttons at the top

The person icon at the top left opens Add Friends, where you look for new helpers. The shield on the right shows your trust score and opens your Trust Score page. The bell opens Updates.

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (1)
text:
The round blue button in the middle of the bar posts a request that nearby helpers can see.

Tip: Nothing is sent until you tap Post Help. You can fill the form in, look at it, and leave the screen without posting anything.

Post a request, step by step

1. Tap the round blue Ask Help button in the middle of the bar at the bottom of the screen.
2. Type a short title in the box called Title, for example "A ride to the clinic on Thursday".
3. Under Kind of help, tap the one that fits best: Company, Rides, Shopping, Cleaning or Other.
4. If you tapped Other, type a few words in the new box called What kind of help?.
5. Under How soon?, leave Normal as it is, or tap Urgent.
6. Add anything a helper should know in the box called Details (optional). You may leave this box empty.
7. Tap Post Help at the bottom of the screen.

The elder's Ask Help form: Title with its hint underneath, the Kind of help row, How soon?, Details (optional), and Post Help held at the bottom.

Ways to reach the form

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (2)
text:
The round blue Ask Help button is the usual way in. Three other screens offer a button that opens the same form when they have nothing to show. Messages offers one when you have no conversations at all. My Helpers offers one when the group you are looking at has nobody in it. Posted Help offers one when Waiting is empty. Each of those buttons reads Ask Help and opens this same page.

Note: The round button belongs to the seat. On a helper account it reads Offer Help and opens a list of requests instead. A family account has no round button.

The Title box

Title must be filled in. Under it sits the hint: Short and clear, like "A ride to the clinic on Thursday". The title is the first line a helper reads, and on your own Posted Help list it is the line you see before you open the request. A day and a place in the title do most of the work.

Tip: Keep the title short. A very long title, past about two hundred letters and spaces, will not post.

The five kinds of help

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (3)
text:
Kind of help offers five answers: Company, Rides, Shopping, Cleaning and Other. Choose the one closest to what you need. Whichever you choose shows as a small label on the request a helper reads. Only one can be chosen. Company is already chosen when the form opens, so this question is never left blank by accident.

The five sit in one row that slides sideways, because five will not fit across a phone. The chosen one turns pale blue and grows a small tick in front of its name. Other sits at the end of the row, past the edge of the screen on a small phone. Pull the row to the left with your finger to reach it.

What Other opens

Choosing Other adds a box called What kind of help? straight under the row. That box has to be filled in as well. Whatever you write in it goes to the top of the words a helper reads on their list, as "Kind of help:" followed by yours. Anything you wrote in Details (optional) follows below it, so nothing you typed is thrown away.

Normal and Urgent

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (4)
text:
How soon? has two answers and Normal is already chosen when the form opens. Choosing Urgent puts a red dot and the word Urgent beside the kind of help on a helper's Offer Help list. On your own list it shows in the small line inside the opened request, which reads like "Rides · Urgent · posted 2 hours ago".

Take care: Urgent does not ring anybody's phone. Posting a request sends no alert to any helper, urgent or not. Helpers see it when they next look at Offer Help. If something is happening right now and you need somebody at once, this form is the wrong door. Use emergency services, or your emergency contacts.

Details, and how much to write

Details (optional) can be left empty and the request still posts. On a helper's list the details show as the first two lines. Put the day, the time, and how long you think it will take in those first two lines. When the details run well past two lines a Read more link appears under them, and tapping it opens the rest.

Tip: Nothing important should sit at the end of a long note. Say it first.

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (5)
text:
How requests look on a helper's Offer Help list. Each one shows its title, the first two lines of the details, a Read more link when there is more, the kind of help, a red Urgent mark when it is urgent, and who posted it.

Tapping Post Help

Post Help is held at the bottom of the screen, above the bar, so it stays in the same place however far you have scrolled. While it is working the button reads Posting… and a small turning circle appears to the left of that word. It will not take a second tap while it is working, so pressing twice cannot post twice.

When it lands, Towinly says "Help posted!" in a small card at the bottom of the screen for four seconds, and moves you to Posted Help. The form empties itself behind you, back to Company and Normal, ready for the next one.

Note: You land on whichever of the three groups you were last looking at on Posted Help. If your new request is not in front of you, tap Waiting. New requests always start there. Your phone gives a short buzz as well, unless you have turned Vibration feedback off in Profile.

When the app says no

Three checks run on your phone the moment you tap Post Help. Nothing is sent while any of them is unhappy.

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (6)
text:
What is wrong | What Towinly says, word for word
Title is empty | Please give your request a short title.
Other is chosen and What kind of help? is empty | Please tell us what kind of help you need.
A word Towinly will not carry | Please take out "…". Towinly is read by older people who are trusting us with their homes.

A refusal appears in red under the box it belongs to, with a small warning mark beside it, and it takes the place of the hint that was there. A screen reader says it out loud once. Your words are never wiped. Change one letter in that box and the red line goes on its own.

Note: A very long title or very long details are refused later, by Towinly's own computers rather than by your phone. The request does not post, and Towinly says so in a small card at the bottom of the screen. Keep the title to a line and the details to a few sentences and this will not happen.

Your location

Take care: With no saved position, helpers who have shared their own location will not see your request at all. This is worth doing once. It is saved as a rounded area, about two kilometres across, never your address, and never while the app is closed.

heading: If you are an elder / Asking for help (7)
text: Note: "Help is easy to find. Trust takes time."

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (1)
text:
What happened to everything you asked for, in three groups.

The second button on the bar is Posted Help. Your requests sit in three groups: Waiting for the ones nobody has been chosen for yet, In Progress for the ones a helper is doing, and Completed for the ones that are finished. Each group carries a count.

Tap a request to open it. You see who has offered, with each helper's name and how far along your friendship with them is. Say yes to the one you would like, and the request moves to In Progress.

A request your family asked for on your behalf is labelled on the card, in words, like "Asked by Sarah, for you". You always know who did what.

The Posted Help screen: the card about your location, the search box, the three groups with their counts, and the requests below. The first one was written by family, so it carries the line "Asked by Sarah, for you".

Note: The first time you open this screen, Towinly asks whether it may use your location. It saves a rounded position, about a two kilometre area, so helpers see roughly how far away you are. It never saves your address, and never looks while the app is closed. Tap Use my location or Not now.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (2)
text:
Your own requests, in three groups

- Waiting holds the requests helpers can still answer.
- In Progress holds the ones where you have chosen a helper.
- Completed holds the ones you marked finished, and the ones you took down.

The card about your location

Until you answer the location question, a card sits at the top of this screen. Its heading reads "Let helpers see how far away you are". Under it: "Towinly can use your location so helpers nearby see how far away you are, instead of the town you typed when you joined. We save a rounded position, about a two kilometre area, never your address. Never while the app is closed." Two answers sit at the bottom of the card: Use my location and Not now.

1. Read the card.
2. Tap Use my location if you want helpers to see how far away you are. Your phone then asks you as well, and you answer that too.
3. Tap Not now to put the card away instead.

Note: Not now hides the card. It can come back later, for example the next time you open Towinly. Your requests work either way. Without a position, a request shows the town you typed when you joined.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (3)
text:
If you say no when your phone asks, the card changes on the spot. Which card you get depends on whether your phone will let Towinly ask again. One reads "Helpers cannot see how far away you are", with the line "Without your location your request shows the town you typed, so a helper on your street looks no closer than one across town. Helpers still see it, and you can turn this on whenever you like." Use my location is still on it. The other reads "Location is turned off for Towinly" and tells you what to do: "To show helpers how far away you are, open Settings on your phone, find Towinly, and turn Location on. Your request still shows without it." That one has no Use my location, because only your phone's own settings can change it. Not now is on both.

Note: If location is switched off for the whole phone, the card reads "Location is turned off on this phone" instead, and says: "Turn Location on in your phone settings and helpers nearby can see how far away you are. Your request still shows without it."

What one request shows

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (4)
text:
A request sits on its own line. The title is the big word on it, like "Ride to my doctor appointment". Two more lines can sit under the title without you touching anything. If a family member wrote the request for you, the line "Asked by Sarah, for you" sits under the title, with their name in it. If you have already chosen a helper, the line under the title names them and says where your friendship stands, like "Ethan Cole · Building trust".

Tap the title and the whole request opens underneath it. The first line inside gives the kind of help, how soon you needed it, and when you asked: "Rides · Normal · posted yesterday". The kind of help is one of Company, Rides, Shopping, Cleaning or Other. A request you marked urgent says "Urgent" in place of "Normal". A request you took down says "Cancelled" at the end of that same line. Tap the title again to fold it away. The small arrow on the right points down while the request is open.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (5)
text:
Note: While helpers are waiting for your answer, a small number sits on the right of the title. It counts the helpers who have offered on that one request. The number in the corner of the small picture above the word Posted Help, on the bar at the bottom, is a different number: it adds up the offers on all of your waiting requests together. Both stay until you accept a helper or take the request down. Opening the screen does not clear either one.

Note: If you allowed Towinly to send notifications, a new offer also shows on your phone. The helper's name is the heading, and the line under it reads "offered to help with your request." The title of your request is never shown there, so nobody reading your locked phone learns what you asked for. Tapping that notification opens Posted Help.

Choosing a helper

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (6)
text: Open a request in Waiting and the offers sit under the details line. A line above them counts the offers in words: "3 helpers want to help". One offer reads "1 helper wants to help". Each helper below has their picture on the left and their name beside it. A helper with no picture shows their initials in a circle instead. If the helper wrote you a message it sits under their name, shortened to two lines; a helper who wrote nothing shows their name alone. Accept sits at the right of their row. Tap the picture or the name to open their profile first, where you can read what they say about themselves and what other people have written about them. A request nobody has answered yet opens to the details line and Remove, with nothing in between.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (7)
text:
1. Tap the request in Waiting to open it.
2. Tap a helper's name to read their profile, then come back.
3. Tap Accept on the row of the helper you want.
4. Read the question. The heading says "Accept this helper?" and the line under it names them and your request: "Ethan Cole will be your helper for "Ride to my doctor appointment"." If that helper wrote you a message, it follows under the words "Their message:", the whole of it, including the part their row was too short to show.
5. Tap Accept to choose them, or Not now to leave things as they are.

Open that request again and your helper has a row of their own inside it. Tap the row to see their profile. The line under their name says where you both stand, like "Building trust · Stage 1 of 7, Connected. Tap to see their profile." For a moment after the screen opens, before your friendships have loaded, that line reads "Is helping you with this. Tap to see their profile." instead.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (8)
text:
Accepting opens a friendship as well. Your helper's name appears on My Helpers. A helper you have never been connected with before starts on the first step of the trust ladder, under Building Trust, and on that first step you cannot type a message to them yet. Their chat says "You're connected. Messages unlock at the next trust step." with Start the next step under it. You are the one who starts it. Tapping it asks "Start the next step?" and explains: "Trust grows only when BOTH of you agree. Ethan Cole will get a tap to accept." Tap Start to send it, or Not yet to wait. Once you have started it, the button is replaced by the line "You've started the next step. Waiting for Ethan Cole to accept.", and messages open when they accept.

Take care: Accepting cannot be undone from this screen. Once a helper is on a request, Remove is gone from it and Mark completed takes its place, and no button swaps one helper for another. If it does not work out, mark the request finished and post a new one.

Marking a request finished

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (9)
text:
1. Tap the request in In Progress to open it.
2. Tap Mark completed, at the bottom right of the opened request.
3. Read the question. The heading says "Mark as completed?" and the line under it says ""Ride to my doctor appointment" will move to your finished requests."
4. Tap Mark completed to confirm, or Not yet to leave it where it is.

Towinly says "Marked as completed. Well done!" at the bottom of the screen and the request moves to Completed. Open it there and your helper is still named, with the line "Helped you with this." underneath. Their row still opens their profile when you tap it. A finished request carries no buttons. Your friendship with that helper carries on. They stay on My Helpers, and your trust steps together are untouched.

Taking a request down

1. Tap the request in Waiting to open it.
2. Tap Remove, at the bottom right of the opened request.
3. Read the question. The heading says "Remove this request?" and the line under it says ""Ride to my doctor appointment" will be taken down. This cannot be undone."
4. Tap Remove to take it down, or Keep it to change your mind.

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (10)
text:
Towinly says "Request removed." at the bottom of the screen. Helpers stop seeing it, and anyone who offered gets no answer from you. The request is not wiped from your own list. It moves into Completed and carries the word "Cancelled" at the end of its details line, so you can still see what you asked for and when.

When a group is empty

Group | The line it shows when nothing is in it
Waiting | "Nothing here yet. Ask your neighbors for a hand. It takes a minute." A button underneath says Ask Help and opens the form.
In Progress | "No requests in progress. When you accept a helper, it moves here."
Completed | "No completed requests yet."

When something does not work

heading: If you are an elder / Posted Help (11)
text:
A tap that does not go through says so at the bottom of the screen, and nothing on the request changes. Accepting shows "Could not accept right now. Please try again." Marking one finished shows "Could not mark completed. Please try again." Removing shows "Could not remove it. Please try again." If your email address is still unconfirmed, all three say "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again." instead. If the whole list cannot load, the screen says "We couldn't load your requests right now. Please check your connection and try again." with a Try again button under it.

Tip: Pull the list down with your finger to look again for new offers. Leaving this screen and coming back does the same thing on its own.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (1)
text:
Up to five people who can see that you are safe. You decide what each of them may see and do.

Open it from Profile, then My Family. The screen has three parts across the top: Controls, My family and How it works.

The Controls page on Sharing. Ethan Cole's line reads Your family can see this friendship. Claire Dubois's reads Kept private from family. Only you can change this.

The four promises

How it works lists them:

- Your family can see you're safe.
- They only see the friendships you choose to share.
- They can never post or act for you.
- You can remove anyone at any time.

Adding somebody

1. Open My family and tap + Add a family member.
2. Type the name they use on Towinly and say how they are related to you.
3. Send it. They have to accept before anything is linked.

Five people is the limit, and requests waiting for an answer count towards it. Having any family connected adds one point to your trust score. It is one point in total, however many people you add.

Sharing: what they can see

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (2)
text:
Every friendship you have starts private. On the Controls tab, under Sharing, there is a switch for each one. Turn a switch on and your family can follow how that friendship is going, read the small group chat on it, and talk to that helper themselves once you and the helper are messaging. Turn it off and the app says "Kept private from family. Only you can change this."

What turning Sharing on gives your family, in the app's own words.

Act for me: what they can do

Three separate permissions, each off until you turn it on, and each set for one family member at a time. They only ever work on a friendship you have already shared.

Switch | What it lets them do
Ask for help for you | Post a request for you, and close one you no longer need. Helpers always see that your family member posted it for you.
Move a friendship forward for you | Take your next trust step with a helper. The step still counts as yours, and your helper sees who took it.
Leave a review for you | Rate a helper you fully trust. The review is yours, with your family member's name on it as the person who wrote it.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (3)
text:
A family member can ask you for one of these. Their request appears on your My family tab under "They're asking you", with Yes and Not now buttons. Nothing changes until you tap Yes.

Take care: Removing somebody takes away everything at once: they stop seeing that you are safe and stop seeing any friendship you shared. If they were your last family member, the family trust point goes too. You can add them again later, and they would have to accept again.

When the app refuses to send

Only one check happens on your phone. Leave the first box empty and red words appear before anything is sent. Every other refusal below comes back from Towinly after the request has already gone, so there is a short wait first. The red words sit under the two boxes, above Send request. They stay on the screen until you tap Send request again.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (4)
text:
Take care: Five is the whole limit, and every request still waiting takes one of the five, whether you sent it or they did. The title keeps the count for you, as in My Family (3/5). At five the + Add a family member button is not shown, and this line takes its place: "You've reached the limit of 5 family members, counting open requests. Remove someone or cancel a request to add another person."

What sits on the My family page, in order

The My family page always reads top to bottom in the same order. First, if a family member has asked you for something, They're asking you. Next the heading People in your family with the + Add a family member button beside it, and the limit line or the open form under it. Then They want to join your family, for people asking to join from their side. Then Requests you sent. Then your people. Until anyone is linked, a small card reads "No family linked yet" and "Add up to 5 people. Each one must accept before they're linked to you."

Somebody asking to join you

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (5)
text:
Anybody can send the request from their side instead. It waits under the heading They want to join your family, on a line like "Daughter · wants to join as your family. It's your choice." Two buttons follow. Accept answers with "They are now part of your family here." Not now answers with "Request declined." These rows never fold away, so the two buttons can never hide behind a tap.

Once anyone is linked, you have your family trust point. More people do not add more. The How it works page says it plainly: "Family connected gives you +1 trust point. One point total, however many family members you add (up to 5 people)."

The rows under People in your family

Note: Main contact is a small pale label with green lettering, sitting beside the relationship when the line is open. Only one person carries it. That person's line shows two buttons, Message and Remove, because there is nothing to promote. Everybody else's line shows three. Giving the label to somebody else takes it off the person who had it.

Removing somebody

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (6)
text:
1. Tap the person's line under People in your family to open it.
2. Tap Remove.
3. Read the box that opens. Its heading is "Remove Sarah from your family?"
4. Tap Remove from family, on the right, to go ahead.

Note: To change your mind, tap Keep on the left of that same box. Touching the dim area around the box does the same.

The box spells out what they lose: "They will no longer see that you're safe or any friendship you shared. If they're your last family member here, your family trust point goes too. You can add them again later. They would need to accept again." When it is done, a message says "Removed from your family."

Take care: Removing takes away more than the box lists. Every Act for me switch you had given that person turns off. Any ask of theirs still waiting for your answer goes with it. If they were holding a key to your Sealed box, that key ends too. Add them again later and every switch starts from off, with nothing carried over.

The Controls page: Sharing and Act for me

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (7)
text:
Controls waits until somebody is actually in your family. Until then it shows one card reading "Add a family member first" and "Once someone is in your family, you choose here what they can see and what they can do for you. Everything starts off." Once a person is linked, the page opens with this line: "Sharing is what your family can see. Act for me is what they can do. Both start off, and only you can change them." Under it are two headings, Sharing and Act for me. The number beside Sharing is how many friendships you have turned on. The number beside Act for me is how many family members have at least one switch on.

Sharing, friendship by friendship

A Sharing switch reaches your whole family at once. The card says so before any switch: "Everyone in your family gets the friendships you turn on here. On a shared friendship they can:" and then lists the four things in plain words.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (8)
text:
- See how the friendship is going, step by step. They cannot change anything.
- Follow the small group chat on it, together with you and your helper.
- Talk to that helper too, once you and your helper are messaging.
- Use anything you allow on the Act for me tab. Those powers only work on friendships you share.

One more line closes that explanation and opens the list of switches: "Turn a friendship off any time. Your family loses all of this straight away." Under it, one row for each friendship: the helper's name, then a switch labelled Let my family see this friendship. Switched on, the words under it read "Your family can see this friendship." Switched off, they read "Kept private from family. Only you can change this."

Note: Only friendships that are going now have a row here. A friendship you paused with Take a break has no row on this page until it starts again. Your family chats are not in this list either, so you can never show one family member to another. With no helper friendships at all, the page says "You have no friendships yet. Once you do, you choose here which ones your family can see."

Act for me, person by person

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (9)
text: This page waits until you have shared at least one friendship. Before that it says "Share a friendship first" and explains: "Your family can only act on a friendship you share with them. Turn on at least one friendship on the Sharing tab, then choose here what they may do for you." After that, every family member gets their own card carrying their name and how they are related to you. Inside it, under the heading Act for me, the app says "Sharing lets Sarah see. These let Sarah act. Each one stays off until you turn it on, and their name is always on whatever they do." The three switches in that card belong to that one person. Give a power to your daughter and your son still has nothing.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (10)
text:
Switch | What it says while it is off | What it says once you turn it on
Ask for help for you | Off. Sarah can see your help requests but cannot change them. | Sarah can ask for help for you, and close a request you no longer need. Helpers always see Sarah asked for you.
Move a friendship forward for you | Off. Sarah can see how a friendship is going but cannot move it on. | Sarah can take your next step with a helper. The step still counts as yours, and your helper sees Sarah took it for you.
Leave a review for you | Off. Sarah cannot leave a review for you. | Sarah can rate a helper you fully trust. The review is yours, with Sarah's name on it as the person who wrote it.

When they ask you for a power

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (11)
text:
A family member can ask you for one of the three from their side. The ask waits at the very top of My family, under the heading They're asking you, written as a line like "Sarah asks: ask for help for you". Under it the app spells out the yes in the same words the switch uses, then adds: "It's your choice, and you can turn it off again any time." Yes answers with "Done. They can do this for you now." Not now answers with "Okay. Nothing changes." The number beside My family counts these asks together with any requests to join, so it is the count of things waiting for your answer.

Note: They can only ask about something they do not already have, and it stays off until you say yes. Anything you turned on for them earlier keeps working while the ask waits. Saying Yes and turning that same switch on yourself are the same act, and turning it on yourself clears the ask from your page. Once you have answered, they cannot ask you about that same thing again for seven days.

heading: If you are an elder / Your family (12)
text: The family member's own page, under the heading What I can do for Margaret. Two of the three read On with the line Margaret lets you do this. The third reads You asked. Waiting for Margaret to decide. They answer on their My Family page.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (1)
text:
Your stories, your letters, and the things only you know. You choose who sees each one.

Open it from Profile, then My boxes. There are three boxes along the top: Story box, Letter box and Sealed box.

Saved stories, newest first: what you wrote this morning is at the top of the page, not the bottom. Each one shows its name, a small word saying who can see it, the story in full, and then the two buttons Change and Remove.

Take care: The app says this at the top of every box: "This is not a will, and it does not replace one." A will decides who gets your money, your home and your things. Nothing here changes any of that. If you have a will, please tell whoever helped you make it that this page exists.

The Story box

A story can be a small one. How you met. What you learned the hard way. The recipe nobody else has. Tap Tell a story, write it, and choose who may read it: anyone, your family, your helpers, or one person. Choosing anyone asks you to confirm, because it means people you have never met.

Take care: Do not put your bank's security answers in the Story box: your first pet, the street you grew up on, your mother's family name. Those belong in the Sealed box.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (2)
text:
The Letter box

A letter goes to one person, and only that person. Tap Write a letter, write it, and choose when it can be read: They can read it now or Only after I'm gone.

Nothing opens on its own. Before a held letter is passed on, a person at Towinly checks a death certificate, asks the people you chose, and tries to reach you for thirty days. Holding a letter until after you are gone needs Keyholders, so the app sends you to the Sealed box first.

The Sealed box

The app describes this box as "Where the money is. Which bank. Where the papers are kept. Write them down once, here." Whatever you put in is locked, and visible to nobody but you. Setting it up takes three steps:

1. Choose at least three people from your family list who could one day ask for the box to be opened. They are called Keyholders. Nobody is asked anything until you finish.
2. Choose how many of them have to agree. The app will not let you pick all of them, so the box can still be opened if one Keyholder cannot be reached.
3. Confirm your email address, make sure you have a password, and save the one-page copy somewhere outside Towinly.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (3)
text:
Each thing in the box shows its name, its kind and the word Locked. See this and Delete sit under every one, with Put something in below the list and Who can open it one day underneath that.

After it is set up, there are seven days when you can undo the whole thing with one button that says "If this was not your idea, undo it". Nobody is told you did that.

To open something you have locked away, tap See this and type your password. The app shows it on the same screen, and Hide this again puts it back.

Take care: The part where your Keyholders can ask to open the box is still being built, and the app says so on the screen. Today the box keeps your notes safe and records who you trust. Nobody can ask to open it yet.

Before you write anything

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (4)
text:
This page is on the elder's side of Towinly. Signed in as a helper or as family, you do not get it at all. The page is called What I pass on. Under the title it says "Your stories, your letters, and the things only you know. You choose who sees each one." Below that sits a short line to read once: "This is not a will, and it does not replace one." Under that line, over on the left, is a small button reading What's the difference?. Tap it and more words open below it: "A will decides who gets your money, your home and your things. Nothing you write on this page changes who gets what. If you have a will, please tell whoever helped you make it that this page exists." Tap it again to close them.

Under that sit three names side by side: Story box, Letter box and Sealed box. Tap one to open it. You can also slide the page left or right with your finger to move between the three. A story goes to whoever you choose, and one of those choices is a single person. A letter always goes to one person and nobody else. The Sealed box is for the things nobody should read while you are alive.

Writing a story, field by field

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (5)
text:
1. Tap Story box at the top of the page.
2. Tap Tell a story.
3. Type a short name in the box marked Give it a name. Before you type, the box shows the example "The winter we lost the roof" in grey.
4. Write the story itself in the box marked Tell it.
5. Tap one answer under Who should see this?.
6. Tap Save this story.

Take care: Under the writing box, every story form shows this warning in green: "Please keep things a bank would ask you out of here: your first pet, the street you grew up on, your mother's family name. Those belong in the Sealed box." A story can be shown to strangers, so anything a bank would use to prove you are you belongs in the Sealed box instead.

The answer you tap | Who that lets in
Anyone | "Anyone who opens your page, including people you have never met."
My family | "Only the family members on your family list."
My helpers | "Only the helpers you have built up trust with."
One person | "One person you choose. Nobody else."

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (6)
text:
My family is already chosen when the form opens. Tapping One person adds a list of names underneath, headed Who is this for?, and you tap the one you mean. Tapping Anyone does nothing more than choose it. The question comes later, when you tap Save this story. A message then asks "Show this to anyone?" and says "Anyone who opens your page can read this, including people you have never met. You can change your mind later." The two buttons are Yes, show it to anyone and Go back. Go back cancels only that save. The form stays open with every word you typed still in it.

Note: That question is asked when you are writing something new. If you go back to a story you already saved and switch it to Anyone, the app does not ask, so read the answer you have chosen before you save.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (7)
text:
Note: An empty Story box reads: "Nothing here yet. A story can be a small one: how you met, what you learned the hard way, the recipe nobody else has." An empty Letter box reads: "No letters yet. A letter goes to one person, and only that person." If you leave a box blank the app will not save and says which one: "Please give it a name.", "Please tell it before you save it." for a story, "Please write something before you save it." for a letter, and "Please choose the one person this is for." when no name is chosen. The name stops at 120 letters and the writing itself at 20,000. A save that works says "Your story is saved." or "Your letter is saved." A save that cannot reach Towinly says "We could not save that. Please try again." and leaves every word you typed on the screen. Cancel at the bottom of the form throws away what you have typed and closes it.

What a saved story or letter shows you

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (8)
text:
- A story shows a small word at the top right saying who can see it: Anyone, My family, My helpers or One person.
- A letter shows the person's name there instead, in the form "To Sarah".
- Under a letter there is a second small word: "Held until after you are gone", or "They can read this now".
- Once that person has opened a letter, a line appears beside that word, for example "Sarah read this on 6 August".
- The whole story or letter is shown in full. Nothing is shortened.

Changing one, or taking it down

Under every saved story and letter sit two small buttons: Change and Remove. Change opens the same form again with your own words already in it, so you can mend a line and save it again. Remove asks first. The question is "Take this down?" and under it: "It will be gone from your page, and nobody will be able to read it." The buttons are Take it down and Keep it. When it has gone the app says "Taken down." Nothing brings it back, so use Change if you only want to fix a word.

The Letter box, one person at a time

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (9)
text:
1. Tap Letter box at the top of the page.
2. Tap Write a letter.
3. Type a short name in the box marked Give it a name. Before you type, the box shows the example "For Sarah" in grey.
4. Write the letter in the box marked Write it.
5. Tap one name under Who is this for?.
6. Tap They can read it now or Only after I'm gone under When can they read it?.
7. Tap Save this letter.

They can read it now is already chosen, and under it the app says "It goes on your page as soon as you save it, for the one person you chose." Under Only after I'm gone it says "Nobody sees this until someone at Towinly has checked a death certificate, asked the people you chose, and tried to reach you for thirty days."

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (10)
text: The names under Who is this for? come from two places and nowhere else: everybody on your family list, each with your word for them on the second line, and any helper who has reached the top of the trust ladder, whose second line reads "Helper you trust". Where you have not recorded a word for a family member, that second line reads "Family". A helper part way up the ladder is not on the list. You cannot type in an address, and you cannot write to somebody who is not already on one of those two lists. When both lists are empty the app says, in place of the names, "There is nobody to write to yet. Add someone to your family list, or build up trust with a helper, and they will appear here." The same list of names is used when a story is for One person.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (11)
text:
Take care: Only after I'm gone stays grey and will not take a tap until your Sealed box is set up. The reason sits under it: "First choose the people who can open things for you, in your Sealed box. Then you can hold a letter until after you are gone.", with Go to my Sealed box below that. A letter you are already holding keeps its hold even if you later undo the Sealed box setup. Going back to fix a spelling in an old held letter will not turn it into one your daughter reads that afternoon.

Note: If Towinly cannot fetch the list of people you may write to, the Write a letter button is not drawn at all. In its place you will see "We couldn't load the people you can write to right now. Please check your connection and try again." with a Try again button. The same calm sentence is used whenever another list on this page fails to arrive, with the name of that list in it: your stories, your letters, your Sealed box, your keyholders, your sealed items, and your family list while you are setting the Sealed box up. Nothing has been lost. Tap Try again when your signal is back.

Setting up the Sealed box, step by step

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (12)
text:
- Step one says under the question: "Pick at least three people you trust. They must already be on your family list, and each one has to say yes before they count."
- Next on step one stays grey until three people are chosen. Once five are chosen the remaining names fade and stop working, and they come back the moment you unchoose one.
- A Keyholder can only be somebody on your family list. Not a helper, however much you trust them, and nobody from outside Towinly. When your family list is too short, step one says "You need at least three people on your family list first." with Go to my family list under it.
- Under the names, step one says "Nobody is asked anything until you finish." That is the truth. Not one of them hears anything until you tap Finish setting this up.
- Step two shows numbers to tap only when you chose four or five people. With four you are offered 2 and 3. With five you are offered 2, 3 and 4. With three people there is only one workable answer, which is two, so no numbers are drawn.
- Under the question, step two explains why it is never all of them: so that one person who is far away, or who has passed on themselves, can never keep it shut forever. Lower down sits the sentence in your own names, along these lines: "So: any 2 of Sarah, David and Ruth. That means 2 of them can open it even if the other one says no."
- Step three shows no Finish setting this up button at all until your email address is confirmed and your account has a password. If your email is not confirmed it asks you to confirm it first, with Go to my account settings. If you signed in with Google it says "Your Sealed box is kept shut by your password, and this account signs in with Google. Please set a password first, then come back."
- Step three also shows "Keep a copy somewhere else" and, under it, "Save your one-page copy to your computer, and keep it wherever your family would think to look. Do not let this app be your only copy."
- The first sentence you mark reads "I understand this is not a will." The second says that Towinly holds the key, so somebody here could open your box, and that this is also why you can never be shut out of it: if you forget your password you reset it as usual. Both sentences come from Towinly rather than from the app on your phone, and Towinly keeps a record that you agreed to those exact words.
- Go back returns to the step before, with your choices still in place. Not now closes the whole thing and keeps none of it.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (13)
text:
The seven days, and the list of answers

The moment you finish, the Sealed box changes. Reading down from the top you get four things. First the line about what is inside, with anything already in the box under it and the button Put something in below that. Second a message headed "Your box is set up." reading: "Nothing can be opened by anyone but you. We will check with you once more in seven days before this is settled, and we have written to" and then your own names, "to ask if they will hold a key." Under that message sits If this was not your idea, undo it. That message and that button are there for seven days and then both go. Third the list headed Who can open it one day, which is there from the first moment and stays for good. Fourth, at the very bottom, the link Save your one-page copy.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (14)
text:
Each person you named is asked on their own Towinly home screen, in the family seat. They read "Margaret has asked you to hold a key." It explains that one day, after you are gone, they would be one of the people who can ask to open your Sealed box, and that they cannot see anything in it now and never will unless that day comes. It also tells them how many of the group would have to agree, and that someone at Towinly would check first. Their two buttons are Yes, I will do that and No thanks, and under them: "You can change your mind whenever you like."

Tapping If this was not your idea, undo it asks "Undo the whole setup?" and says "Your box stays exactly as it is, and everything you wrote stays where it is. The people you asked will stop being asked, and nobody is told you did this." The buttons are Yes, undo it and Leave it as it is. Afterwards the app says "That is undone. Nobody is holding a key."

What goes in the box

The place to put things in only appears once you have finished setting the box up. Before that, the Sealed box holds the long message described above and the single button Set this up. There is no way to put anything in until the setup is done.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (15)
text:
1. Tap Put something in.
2. Type a name in the box marked What is it?. Before you type, the box shows the example "Where the money is" in grey.
3. Write the thing itself in the box marked Write it down.
4. Tap Money, Passwords, Papers or Something else under What kind of thing is it?.
5. Tap Lock this away.

The line above the list counts what is inside: "Your box is shut. 3 things are inside. Nobody can see them but you." While the box is set up but still empty, it reads "Your box is shut. There is nothing in it yet. Nobody can see what you put in but you." Above the name box, the form promises "Give it a name you would recognise. Nobody else ever sees this name, not even your Keyholders." A save that works says "That is locked away." If you leave something out, the app says which: "Please give it a name.", "Please write something before you save it.", or "Please choose what kind of thing this is." There is no way to edit. Nothing in the box can be changed once it is locked. To correct something, take it out and put a new one in.

Reading something back

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (16)
text:
1. Tap See this under the thing you want to read.
2. Type your Towinly password in the box marked Your password.
3. Tap Show it to me.

A short section opens under that same thing saying "Type your password to see this." Your words then appear on the screen, the word Locked changes to Open, and a button Hide this again puts them away. Never mind closes the section and opens nothing. The words are on the screen only while you are looking at them. They are gone the moment you tap Hide this again or leave the page, and nothing is kept on the phone.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (17)
text:
Note: If you leave the password box empty you get "Please type your password." A wrong password gets "That password was not right. Please try again." After five wrong tries the app stops you: "That password has been tried too many times. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." And for seven days after you change your Towinly password the box will not open at all. It says "You changed your password recently. For your safety your Sealed box stays shut until", then a real date, then "If that was not you, tell us straight away.", followed by where to write to Towinly. That week is there on purpose. It gives you time to notice if somebody else changed your password.

Your one-page copy

At the very bottom of the Sealed box, under the list of people, is a link reading Save your one-page copy. It appears only once the box is set up. This is the page you keep outside Towinly, so that your family can find things even if this app is gone.

1. Tap Save your one-page copy at the bottom of the Sealed box.
2. Tap Save a copy of this page.
3. Choose where to send it from the list your phone opens.

heading: If you are an elder / What you pass on (18)
text:
Note: What leaves the app is the words themselves, as plain writing. No file is made on the phone. If you close that list without choosing anywhere, nothing is sent and the line saying when you last saved a copy does not change.

The one-page copy. The line saying whether you have saved one, and the button under it, sit at the top. Everything below the words This is what you will save is what the copy contains.

The page opens with "This is the copy you keep outside Towinly. Save it, and put it wherever your family would think to look. Do not let this app be your only copy." Under that it says either "You have not saved a copy yet." or "You last saved a copy on 29 August 2026." When it has gone out, the app says "Saved. Now put it somewhere your family would look."

Tip: Send yourself a fresh copy whenever you put something new in the box or change who holds a key. The copy is made from what is true on the day you save it, and an old one in a drawer will not know about the rest.

heading: If you are a helper / My Elders, your home screen (1)
text:
Everyone you are building a friendship with, and how far each one has come.

The first button on the bar at the bottom is My Elders. It holds a card for every elder you are connected to, in two groups: Trusted Elders for the friendships that have reached the top of the ladder, and Building Trust for the ones still climbing. Tap either name to switch between them.

Each row shows their photo, or their initials, and their name. Tap a row to open it. Inside you see which of the seven steps you are on together, the trust points earned, and anything waiting for you to answer. Tap a name or photo to open that person's profile.

My Elders. Trusted Elders and Building Trust, with a card for each person.

Trust steps come to you

The elder always starts a trust step. You accept it. There is no button on your side to start one, by design, and that is the whole point of the ladder.

1. When an elder starts a step, their card shows Accept the next step.
2. Tap it. Towinly asks "Accept the next step?" and explains that accepting climbs the ladder for both of you.
3. Tap Accept to agree, or Not yet to leave it.

heading: If you are a helper / My Elders, your home screen (2)
text:
When there is nothing waiting, the card says so in a plain line rather than showing a button you cannot use: the elder starts each step, and you will get a tap here to accept.

Pausing or ending

An open card has Take a break, which pauses trust steps and messages until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost. There is also End, which asks you to confirm and cannot be undone.

heading: If you are a helper / Offering help (1)
text:
The round blue button in the middle shows every open request near you.

Tap the round Offer Help button in the middle of the bar at the bottom. Each card shows the request, the kind of help, who posted it, and how long ago. An urgent request is marked Urgent. A long description is folded, with Read more to open it and Show less to fold it again.

A request a family member posted for their parent says so on the card, in words: "Asked by Sarah, for Margaret". You always know who you are dealing with.

1. Read the request.
2. Tap Offer to Help on that card.
3. Write a short message saying how you could help, and send it.
4. The elder sees your offer on their Posted Help screen and chooses.

Three open requests: cleaning for Grace Liu, a lift Sarah asked for on Margaret's behalf, and an urgent ride. No card here shows a distance.

If they say yes, a chat opens between you and the job moves into In Progress on your My offers & jobs screen. If they choose somebody else, Towinly tells you the request went to someone else this time.

The three lists across the top

heading: If you are a helper / Offering help (2)
text:
Note: Completed gathers every request you offered on that has since been finished, including ones somebody else was chosen for. The number there is a count of requests, never a count of jobs you did.

What each card tells you

A request can be posted with a name and nothing written under it. That card simply has no description line.

A long description is folded to two lines with Read more underneath. Tap Read more and the whole description opens, however long it is. Show less folds it back to two lines.

Take care: A description has to run past about 120 letters and spaces before Read more appears, and two lines hold rather less than that. So a request that runs a little past two lines can be trimmed with no Read more under it. If a card seems to stop mid sentence and there is no Read more, the rest cannot be opened from this screen.

An urgent request carries a small red dot and the word Urgent beside the kind of help. It means the person needs it soon. It does not move the card higher up the list.

Distance, and the button that sets it

heading: If you are a helper / Offering help (3)
text:
The small button at the right of that line steps through 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 km. It starts at 25 km and goes back to 5 km after 100 km. Tapping it asks Towinly for the list again at the new distance.

Note: That line and that distance button belong to Available alone. Applied and Completed have neither.

Offering to help

There is nothing to write. Offering is that one tap, and no message goes with it. What the person receives is your name and your profile, so keep your profile worth reading. If they have notifications turned on, their phone shows your name and the words "offered to help with your request."

If your phone cannot reach Towinly, the message reads "Could not send your offer. Please try again." and the card is left exactly as it was, so you can tap again. If the request already has a helper, or you have offered on it once before, the message is the two plain words "Invalid request." Any of these sits near the bottom of the screen for about four seconds and then goes.

After you have offered

heading: If you are a helper / Offering help (4)
text:
The card turns up under Applied straight away. Whether it also leaves Available depends on your phone. If your phone has never given its location, it goes at once. If it has, the card stays in Available with its Offer to Help button until you pull the list down, and then it goes.

In Applied, the Offer to Help button is replaced by a few words about where your offer stands.

What the card says | What it means
Waiting to hear back | Your offer is in and nobody has answered yet. Under it is the line "The elder reviews all helpers and picks one."
You're helping | They chose you. This one is yours to do, and the words are in green.

Take care: When the elder picks somebody else, the card stays in Applied and the Offer to Help button comes back on it. Nothing on the card says you were turned down. Tapping that button again does not work: Towinly answers "Invalid request.", because the request has its helper now.

Note: If the elder calls the request off, it leaves Applied with nothing said and turns up in no other list. If the request is finished, the card moves to Completed, where it is faded, carries a green Completed label and has no button.

When a list is empty

heading: If you are a helper / Offering help (5)
text: Take care: A quiet list and a lost connection are never given the same words. When nothing can be loaded at all, that place is taken by "We couldn't load open requests near you right now. Please check your connection and try again." with a Try again button under it. On a phone that has given no location the same sentence says "open requests", and on Applied and Completed it says "your offers". Seeing any of them, tap Try again rather than assuming nobody needs help today.

heading: If you are a helper / My offers and jobs (1)
text:
Everything you have offered on, in three groups.

Which group a row sits in

Towinly decides the group for you. You never move a row by hand. Two things settle it: what the elder has said about your offer, and what has happened to the request itself.

Group | What puts a row there | What the row shows before you open it
Waiting | Your offer is sent, the request is still open, and the elder has not answered yet. | The title of the request, on its own.
In Progress | The elder said yes to you, and the request is now yours to do. | The title, and under it the elder's name with where your trust stands.
Completed | The job is finished, or the elder took the request down, or it went to another helper. | A job you did keeps the elder's name and where trust stands under the title. An offer that did not go your way shows the title on its own.

The number beside each group name is how many rows are inside it. A group with nothing in it shows 0 and stays where it is, so the three names never move about. Inside a group, the offer you made most recently sits at the top.

heading: If you are a helper / My offers and jobs (2)
text:
Waiting and In Progress each have a sentence when they are empty that names the thing which would fill them. Waiting says "No offers waiting. Offer to help with a request and it will show up here." In Progress says "Nothing in progress. When an elder says yes to your offer, it moves here." Completed says only "No finished jobs yet."

Opening a row

The Waiting group. One offer, its title on its own, with an arrow at the right that opens it.

- The kind of help is one of five words: Company, Rides, Shopping, Cleaning or Other.
- How soon it was wanted is either Urgent or Normal. Every request says one or the other, so nothing is left for you to guess.
- If the elder has taken the request down, Taken down is added to the end of that same line.

The elder, and where trust stands

The same standing rides on the folded row once the elder has said yes, so you can see who a job belongs to without opening anything. It reads "Margaret · Building trust", and becomes "Margaret · Trusted elder" when you reach the last step together. On a slow connection the row can show the name on its own for a moment, until where trust stands catches up.

How a row moves

heading: If you are a helper / My offers and jobs (3)
text:
1. Tap Offer to Help on the Offer Help screen. The request appears here under Waiting.
2. Wait. The elder reads every offer and picks one person.
3. If they pick you, the row moves itself to In Progress and the elder's name appears on it. Your phone shows their name and the words "accepted your offer to help.", if you have notifications turned on.
4. Do the job. Use Message to agree the details.
5. When the job is marked finished, the row moves to Completed.

If the elder picks somebody else, or takes the request down before anyone is chosen, the row moves to Completed too. Every offer you make stays here in one of the three groups until you withdraw it. A withdrawn offer leaves this screen for good.

You cannot take back an offer from this screen. Withdrawing lives on the Offer Help screen: open it, tap Applied across the top, find the request, and tap Withdraw my offer. The request then leaves Applied and joins the Available group again, with Offer to Help on it, ready if you change your mind.

Note: If your phone has shared where it is, the request may not appear under Available straight away. Pull that screen down with your finger and it comes back.

heading: If you are a helper / My offers and jobs (4)
text:
Take care: Nothing on this screen changes a job. Opening a row only shows you more of it. Choosing a helper and marking a job finished happen on the elder's side, done by the elder or by a family member they have trusted with their help requests. This screen is your record of where each of your offers stands.

Pull the screen down with your finger to fetch your offers again. You can also swipe the list sideways to move between Waiting, In Progress and Completed instead of tapping the names. If the list cannot load, Towinly says so plainly: "We couldn't load your jobs right now. Please check your connection and try again.", with a Try again button underneath.

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (1)
text:
Some elders write down stories and letters. If one chose to share with you, it is on their profile.

Open an elder's profile and look for the row that says What {name} passes on, with the line "Her stories, and any letter she wrote to you." underneath. Tap it.

One elder's page as a helper reads it: From Rose Martin at the top, her line under it, then a story with its name and the whole of it, and Report this below.

The page shows only what that person chose to share with you, and nothing else. A letter addressed to you is marked "A letter for you". If they have not shared anything, the page tells you so.

Note: Nothing from an elder's Sealed box can ever appear here. The Sealed box is kept somewhere this page cannot read.

If something on the page is wrong or upsetting, Report this at the bottom sends it to Towinly with a reason you choose.

Getting to the page

These first steps are for a helper. Signed in as a helper, your first tab at the bottom of the screen reads My Elders.

A family member watching over a parent has no My Elders tab, and no way in from their own list of parents. Their route runs through the chat.

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (2)
text:
1. Tap My Parents at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap your parent's name. The row opens.
3. Tap See Margaret, which carries your own parent's name.
4. Tap Message Margaret near the top of that page. The chat opens.
5. Tap your parent's name and photo at the top of the chat. Their profile opens.
6. Tap the row What Margaret passes on.

What the page shows

The top of the page says From Rose Martin, and under it one line: "What Rose Martin chose to share with you." Then come the cards, the newest first. Each card gives the name she put on the piece of writing, then the whole of it. Nothing is shortened. To load the page again, pull it down with your finger. If it will not load, a calm card says "We couldn't load this page right now. Please check your connection and try again." and offers Try again.

Why one thing is there and another is not

Every time she saves a story or a letter, she picks who it is for. Towinly checks that choice against you, one piece of writing at a time, at the moment you open the page.

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (3)
text:
What she chose | Whether it reaches you
Anyone | Anyone signed in to Towinly can read it, including people she has never met.
My family | Only the people on her family list, and only while that family link is live.
My helpers | Only a helper who has reached the last of the seven steps with her, in a friendship that has not ended and is not paused.
One person | The one person she named, and nobody else. Not her family either.

"My helpers" is a high bar. A friendship a week old does not open it. It has to be a live friendship standing at the top of the seven steps. Nothing is copied to you and kept. If that friendship ends or is paused, or she takes the writing down, her "My helpers" writing is gone from your page the next time you open it.

A letter for you

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (4)
text:
A letter is written to one person. If one is sitting on your page, it was written to you, and it is marked beside its name with the words "A letter for you". A story carries no such mark. The first time a letter written to you reaches your screen, Towinly writes that date down once and shows it to her on her own page, as "Ethan Cole read this on 3 June". Opening the letter again later never moves that date, and her own reading of her page never sets one.

Some letters are held until after the writer is gone. None of those reach your page until somebody at Towinly has finished the handover by hand. Nothing opens on a timer, and there is no button anywhere that opens one. Before a held letter is passed on, a person at Towinly reads a death certificate, asks the people she chose one at a time, and tries to reach her for thirty days.

Reporting a story

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (5)
text:
1. Tap Report this at the bottom of that story's card.
