2. Answer "What is wrong with it?" by tapping one of the four cards. The first one is already chosen for you, so change it if it is not the right one.
3. Add anything you want to say under "Tell us more (you can skip this)". You can leave it empty.
4. Tap Send this to Towinly. To back out instead, tap Never mind.

The four answers are "It says something untrue about me", "It should not be shown to people", "It is unkind or hurtful" and "Something else". While it goes, the button reads Sending…. When it is done, the button on that card is gone and in its place is the line "Thank you. Somebody at Towinly will read this."

If it does not go, the form stays open and says what went wrong. Usually that is "We could not send that. Please try again." If she has taken that story down, or the friendship has dropped off the top step while your form was open, it says "We couldn't find that writing" instead.

heading: If you are a helper / What an elder passes on (6)
text:
Note: Only one report form is open at a time. Starting one on a second story closes the first, and whatever you had typed in it goes. If you leave the page and come back, the Report this button is there again, and your report is already with Towinly.

Take care: A report is read by a person and acted on. It names the story and the person who wrote it, so use it when something is genuinely wrong. Letters carry no Report this button at all. A letter went to you and to nobody else, so nothing in it was shown to other people.

The Sealed box stays out of this

Nothing from an elder's Sealed box can reach this page. Sealed things are kept apart, in a place this page never looks at, and the rule for them says no to every reader. It says no to the writer too. She opens her own sealed things by typing her password, every single time, on her own screen.

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (1)
text:
Everyone you are linked to, and anything new about them.

The family home screen. Margaret's row is folded to her name, with the family news below it.

A family account has three buttons on the bar at the bottom: My Parents, Messages and Profile. There is no round button in the middle, because family never post a request or offer help. That belongs to the elder and the helper.

My Parents has two parts across the top: Parents, for the people you are already linked to, and Requests, for links waiting to be accepted. Each parent's row shows their name and photo, and a small button that opens their own page.

Under that row the heading reads My Parents. A search box appears once you have at least one parent, or one request waiting either way. It narrows the Parents and Requests lists by name, and it leaves the news lower down the screen exactly as it was. If no name matches, the app writes No matches for and your own words back, so you know it looked and found nobody.

One parent's row

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (2)
text:
Under that line the row shows the day's news about them: Checked in today or No check-in yet today, and how many help requests they have open when there are any. That line is fetched on its own, so it can be slow to arrive, and it stays away altogether if it does not arrive at all. Last comes a button reading See and their name, which opens their own page. That button is there either way. Touch the name again to fold the row shut.

Take care: No check-in yet today is grey, and it is not an alarm. Plenty of people check in late in the day, or not at all. Towinly never colours that line red.

Linking to a parent

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (3)
text:
Before you are linked to anybody, the Parents list says No parent linked yet and They must accept before you're linked., with its own Add your parent button. Add parent at the top left opens the same short form, headed Add your parent. Under the title it says: Type their exact Towinly username, email or phone. They must say yes before you see anything. There are two boxes. The first is Username, email or phone, and what you type has to match exactly what your parent uses on Towinly. Your own phone will not offer to fill this one in for you, because it is asking about somebody else. The second is Relationship (what you are to them), with the examples Daughter, Son, Niece. You may leave the second box empty.

1. Touch Add parent at the top left of the screen.
2. Type your parent's exact Towinly username, email or phone number in the first box.
3. Type what you are to them in the second box, such as Daughter. You may leave this box empty.
4. Touch Send request. The app answers Request sent. You become family here once they accept.

Note: Cancel closes the form at any point before the last step. Nothing is sent.

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (4)
text:
If the request will not go, the reason appears in red just above Send request. These are the words you may see.

A request that is still waiting

- A request your parent sent you sits under the heading They added you as family. That row never folds shut, so its two buttons can never hide. It reads their name, then wants you as their family here. Where they wrote what you are to them, words like (as their daughter) follow, and where they left that box empty nothing follows. The line ends It's your choice. Accept links you, and the app says You're now linked as their family. Not now turns it down, and the app says Request declined.
- A request you sent sits under the heading Requests you sent and reads Waiting for Margaret to accept. Only they can say yes. You can cancel any time. One button sits under it: Cancel request. It takes the request back straight away and the app says Request cancelled. You can send a new one later. While a request waits, the row carries their name and nothing at all about their day.

When neither list has anything in it, the Requests list says No requests right now. When you add a parent, or a parent adds you, it waits here until someone says yes.

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (5)
text:
News about your family

Under the two lists is News about your family. The line beneath that heading says Alerts appear here when something needs your attention. Nothing is sent by text or email. Read it as written: no text message and no email goes out to you. The same news also arrives under Updates at the top right, and it is counted in the number on that button.

The app looks for new news about every half minute while you have this screen open. On this list nothing is marked as read, and nothing disappears once you have seen it. The newest twenty are shown, and a button reading Show 6 older alerts, carrying the real number, brings up the rest. The line that explains a kind of news appears on the first row of that kind only. When there is nothing at all, the app says No alerts right now and calls that good news.

The news list further down the same screen. Three notices about Margaret's Sealed box, and one first meeting she chose to share.

Being asked to hold a key

heading: If you are family / My Parents, your home screen (6)
text:
If a parent has asked you to hold a key to their Sealed box, a card sits under the My Parents heading, above the search box and the parent list. When nobody has asked, there is no card and no empty space where one would be.

The card is headed Margaret has asked you to hold a key. and says that one day, after they are gone, you would be one of the people who can ask to open their Sealed box, and that you cannot see anything in it now and never will unless that day comes. If your parent has already settled how many keyholders would have to agree, a second line gives the two real numbers and says someone here at Towinly would check first. Until those numbers are real, that line is left out rather than guessed at. Two buttons sit side by side, the same size on purpose so neither one looks like the easy answer: Yes, I will do that and No thanks. Under them the card says You can change your mind whenever you like.

Tip: Only somebody already linked as family can be asked to hold a key. No outside friend, no helper, nobody else. Your parent may ask up to five people, and may take any key back at any time, on their own, without the app telling anyone.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (1)
text:
How they are today, the friendships they share with you, and what you are allowed to do.

Tap the small button on your parent's row to open their page. At the top are their photo, their name, how you are related, and a label saying Checked in today or No check-in yet today. A full-width button opens a chat with them.

The top of the page and the Friendships part. Margaret shares one friendship, with Ethan Cole at Stage 6 of 7.

Friendships

The friendships your parent has chosen to share with you. Your parent decides which ones, one switch at a time, and everything starts off. For each shared friendship you can see which of the seven steps it is on. You cannot change any of it.

The top of the page

Under the name sits one small label: Checked in today with a tick, or No check-in yet today with a clock face. The second one is plain grey on purpose. The app only asks whether they have checked in at some point today. There is no hour to watch for, and a grey label means nothing more than not yet today.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (2)
text:
Below that is the only button filled in solid blue, Message Margaret. Several other things further down the page are written in blue lettering, so look for the solid blue block. It opens a private chat between the two of you, and reopens that same chat every time after. Being linked is the only permission it needs, and no trust step has to be reached first. While it opens, the button reads Opening….

Note: The check-in label and the whole Today part come from a second reading the phone fetches on its own. If that reading does not arrive, the check-in label is simply missing from the top, and Today shows We couldn't load how Margaret is doing right now. Please check your connection and try again. with a Try again button. While that is happening, Friendships reads as though nothing is shared. Tap Try again before believing it.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (3)
text:
Three parts sit across the middle: Friendships, Today and What I can do. Friendships is the one that opens first. Tap a part to switch, or swipe the page below the row of three names, left or right. That swipe has to be a firm sideways drag. A short one, or one that slants up or down, does nothing. The photo, the name, the check-in label, Message Margaret and the row of names themselves ignore a swipe. Only Today ever carries a number beside its name, and only when your parent has at least one help request open. The other two never carry one.

Friendships

The part opens with the heading Friendships shared with you and the line Margaret chooses which friendships you see here. Below it is one card for each friendship your parent has chosen to share. They decide each one on their own phone, one switch at a time, and every friendship starts off. The card is a window on the friendship. It gives you no way into the private messages your parent and their helper send each other, and no way for you to move the friendship along, unless your parent has turned that on for you by name.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (4)
text:
A link reading Open the group chat is drawn on every shared card. It is the small thread your parent, their helper and you read together, and it only lets you in once the two of them have reached step 6 of 7, Ready to Meet. Tap it earlier and you land on a screen saying We couldn't load your messages right now. Please check your connection and try again. Nothing is broken. The step has not been reached.

When your parent and the helper reach Messaging, step 2 of 7, your parent's trust reaches you too. A green line says You hold Margaret's trust with Ethan. You can message them directly. and three small buttons appear: Message Ethan, Pause and Remove. You send no request and the helper accepts nothing. Under them a line says Margaret always sees that you two can talk. If Margaret stops sharing this friendship, the chat closes.

Today

The Today part as a family member who has been given Ask for help for you sees it: the check-in, three open requests, a close button under each one, and Ask for help for Margaret at the foot. Without that permission the same list carries no buttons.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (5)
text:
Acting on the list is a permission. Without Ask for help for you there are no buttons at all, and if your parent also has nothing open, this part shows only How Margaret is today and the check-in. With the permission a gold line says Margaret asked you to handle these for them. Helpers always see your name next to theirs on anything you do here. Each request then gains Close this request for Margaret. Tapping it asks Close this for Margaret? Helpers will stop seeing it. and waits for Yes, close it or Keep it. If she has nothing open, the part reads Margaret has no open help requests right now.

Note: A request you write goes out as your parent's own. The form says so in gold before you send: This goes out as Margaret's request, with your name on it as the person who asked.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (6)
text:
1. Tap Ask for help for Margaret at the foot of the list.
2. Answer the first box, What does Margaret need help with?
3. Add anything else in the box below, Anything else a helper should know? (optional). You may leave it empty.
4. Under What kind of help?, Company is already chosen for you. Change it to Rides, Shopping, Cleaning or Other if that fits better.
5. Under How soon does Margaret need it?, Normal is already chosen for you. Change it to Urgent if she needs it sooner.
6. Tap Send for Margaret.

Tip: To drop the whole thing without sending, tap Never mind beside the send button. If you leave the first box empty, nothing is sent and a red line says Please write what Margaret needs help with.

What I can do

Under that, What I can do for Margaret lists the three permissions, one row each: Ask for help for you, Move a friendship forward for you and Leave a review for you. Above them sits the reminder Margaret decides each of these, and anything you do carries your name.

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (7)
text:
- A permission your parent has given shows a green On and the line Margaret lets you do this.
- One you have asked for shows Waiting and the line You asked. Waiting for Margaret to decide. They answer on their My Family page.
- One you have not asked for shows a button reading Ask Margaret and the line Not on yet. You can ask Margaret. On the review row, and only while it has not been asked for, that line goes on: Reviews unlock when a friendship is fully trusted.

The four things sharing gives you, then the three permissions. Two are on. Leave a review for you has been asked for and is waiting on Margaret's answer.

Two of the three only work on a friendship your parent has already shared with you: moving a friendship forward, and leaving a review. Asking for help is different. It acts on your parent's own help requests, which belong to no friendship, so it works even when nothing has been shared with you.

When your parent has shared nothing

heading: If you are family / Your parent's page (8)
text:
Friendships then shows its heading and its usual line, followed by No friendships shared with you yet. When Margaret shares one, you can: and the same four lines. That is the page working properly. Nothing is broken and nothing has gone missing. Today still shows the check-in and any open help requests, because those never depended on sharing. What I can do still lets you ask for a permission.

If the link itself has gone, the page carries no parts at all. It says This parent is no longer linked to you and This link may have been removed. with one button, Back to My Parents. Your parent can end a link whenever they choose, and they do not have to tell you first.

Take care: A page that cannot load is not the same as a link that has gone. When the phone cannot reach the app at all, the page says We couldn't load your parent's page right now. Please check your connection and try again. with a Try again button. Only the words above, This parent is no longer linked to you, mean the link has really ended.

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (1)
text:
Three permissions, each one off until your parent turns it on for you by name.

Permission | What it lets you do
Ask for help for you | Post a help request for your parent, and close one they no longer need. Helpers always see that you posted it for them.
Move a friendship forward for you | Take your parent's next trust step with a helper. The step counts as theirs, and the helper sees that you took it.
Leave a review for you | Rate a helper your parent fully trusts. The review is your parent's, and it carries your name as the person who wrote it.

Note: A permission only ever works on a friendship your parent has already shared with you. Sharing comes first, always.

Asking for a permission

This chapter is for a family member's own account. Your parent decides what you may do for them, and can take it back at any time. There are three permissions, and all three are asked for in the same place: Ask for help for you, Move a friendship forward for you and Leave a review for you.

1. Tap My Parents at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap your parent's name in the list. The row opens.
3. Tap See {parent}.
4. Tap What I can do. The three tabs sit under the Message {parent} button.

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (2)
text:
The three permissions are listed under the heading What I can do for {parent}, with one line above them: {parent} decides each of these, and anything you do carries your name. Each row ends in one of three things. A green On with a tick means your parent has allowed it, and the row reads {parent} lets you do this. A grey Waiting means you have asked and they have not answered yet. A button reading Ask {parent} means you can ask.

1. Find the permission you want and tap Ask {parent}.
2. Read the line that appears under it: You asked. Waiting for {parent} to decide. They answer on their My Family page.
3. Wait. Nothing changes until your parent answers.

Note: Asking gives you nothing by itself. It puts a card in front of your parent and stops there. Towinly does not text them or email them about it, so the card waits on their page until they next open the app. Once they have answered, whether the answer was yes or no, you cannot ask about that same permission again for seven days.

Sarah's What I can do page for Margaret. Two permissions say On. The third says Waiting while Margaret decides.

Your parent answers on their own phone, on their own account.

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (3)
text:
1. On their phone, your parent taps Profile at the bottom of the screen.
2. They tap My Family.
3. They tap My family at the top of that page. It opens on Controls, so this tap is needed. The number beside My family counts what is waiting on their answer.
4. Under the heading They're asking you they tap Yes or Not now.

Posting a help request for them

With the permission on, a line in gold sits under the heading: {parent} asked you to handle these for them. Helpers always see your name next to theirs on anything you do here. If your parent has no open request and has not given you this permission, the whole section is missing rather than sitting there empty.

Tip: The first field cannot be left empty. If you try, the app answers: Please write what {parent} needs help with. The faint grey words already sitting in that field are an example. You do not have to type them.

Three open requests for Margaret, each with Close this request for Margaret under it, and Ask for help for Margaret at the bottom.

Closing a request

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (4)
text:
1. Open the Today tab on your parent's page.
2. Find the request and tap Close this request for {parent}.
3. Read the question: Close this for {parent}? Helpers will stop seeing it.
4. Tap Yes, close it. To leave the request open, tap Keep it.

Taking a trust step for them

Two more things have to be true before you can do this, on top of the permission. Your parent has to have shared that friendship with family, because only shared friendships appear on the Friendships tab at all. And the friendship has to be below the top of the trust ladder. At stage 7 of 7 there is no next step to take, so no button is drawn.

1. Open the Friendships tab on your parent's page.
2. Find the helper's card and tap Move the next step forward for {parent}.
3. Read the question: Take {parent}'s next step with {helper's first name}? The step counts as theirs.
4. Tap Yes, move it for {parent}. To leave the friendship alone, tap Not now.

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (5)
text:
Take care: You are taking your parent's half of the step. The friendship only climbs once the helper accepts it as well. If your parent has already taken this step themselves, the app refuses rather than counting it twice: You have already confirmed the current trust level.

Ethan Cole's card on the Friendships tab. Anything you do here is in Margaret's name sits at the bottom of the card, just above the button.

Writing a review for them

A review is worth up to 5 of the 15 trust points that helper can earn with your parent, one point per star. Three stars is worth 3. Only your parent's newest review of that helper counts.

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (6)
text:
1. Open the Friendships tab and find the friendship at stage 7 of 7.
2. Tap Leave a review for {parent}.
3. Read the question at the top of the card: How has {helper's first name} been for {parent}?
4. Set the stars. Five are filled to begin with, so tap a lower star if that is not your answer.
5. Write a few words in A few words (optional), or leave it empty.
6. Read the line above the buttons: This is saved as {parent}'s review, with your name on it as the person who wrote it.
7. Tap Save for {parent}. To close the card without saving, tap Never mind.
8. The card is replaced by one line: Review saved for {parent}, with your name on it.

Take care: Your words are checked before they are sent. If they are refused, the reason appears under the field, nothing is saved, and your stars and your words stay on screen so you can change them.

What the helper sees

heading: If you are family / Doing things for your parent (7)
text:
What you did for your parent | What the helper sees
Posted a help request | The request on their Offer Help list in your parent's name, with a line in gold under it: Asked by your name, for your parent.
Closed a request | It leaves the Offer Help list. No new helper can offer for it.
Took a trust step | A blue Accept the next step button on their card. Tapping it asks Accept the next step? and says your parent has asked to move one step up, and that accepting climbs the ladder for both of you.
Wrote a review | Stars and your words on their own Profile, with no name under them. Anyone who opens their profile page sees the same review with by your parent below it.

Note: Your parent sees a request you posted on their own list too, written as Asked by your name, for you.

Note: On the phone the helper is told your parent asked for the step. Nothing on the helper's screens says which of you tapped it. On the Towinly website a review also carries the line written by your name.

A helper's own Profile. Reviews show the stars and the words, with no name.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (1)
text:
Seven steps. Both people have to agree to every one of them, and nobody can skip any.

Every friendship in Towinly sits on one of seven steps. A friendship starts at the bottom and climbs only when both people say yes. This is what the app means by Help is easy to find. Trust takes time.

Step | Name | What it means
1 | Just Connected | You both said yes. You can see each other's profile.
2 | Messaging | Private messages and photos, inside Towinly. The Message button appears here.
3 | Phone Ready | You both agree to share phone numbers and call each other.
4 | Video Ready | A video call. You meet face to face on a screen.
5 | Social Media | You each share your Instagram, Facebook or other profiles.
6 | Ready to Meet | You plan to meet in person. Emergency contacts are told.
7 | Fully Trusted | The top of the ladder. You can leave and receive reviews.

Note: The elder always starts a step. The helper accepts it. A helper cannot move a friendship on by themselves, and the app will not let them try.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (2)
text:
Three steps change what the app itself allows. Until step 2, the chat has no box to type in. At step 3, phone numbers become visible to each other. At step 6, your emergency contacts are sent a text message when you agree to meet in person for the first time.

Where you see the ladder

Open anyone's row on your home screen. The row unfolds and the ladder is drawn across it as seven dots, from Connected at one end to Trusted at the other, with the step you are on filled in and the next one named.

A friendship opened. Stage 1 of 7, the seven dots, and the buttons for this seat.

Under the dots the app writes the same thing in words: which stage of seven you are on, how many of the 15 trust points this friendship has earned, and the date you connected. If a job is going on, it names that too.

The line under the ladder tells you whose turn it is. On a helper's phone it reads "{Name} starts each trust step. You'll get a tap here to accept." until the elder starts one. On an elder's phone there is a Start the next step button instead.

Message opens your chat with that person, once the friendship has reached step two. Take a break pauses the friendship, and End ends it for good.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (3)
text:
A row before you touch it

Above the rows sit two headings side by side, Building Trust and Trusted Elders on the helper's screen, Building Trust and Trusted Friends on the elder's. Only one list shows at a time. Touch a heading to see that list, or swipe the list sideways.

The helper's list, headed My Elders. Under the heading is the search box, then the two headings Building Trust and Trusted Elders side by side. Below them two rows folded shut: Rose Martin, then David Chen, whose circle carries the initials DC.

What an open row shows on the elder's screen

Some of these lines only appear when there is something to put in them, so an open row is shorter on the day it has less to say.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (4)
text:
- The step, written "Stage 4 of 7 · Video". The short word is used here. In sentences the same step is called "Video Ready".
- Why this friendship exists and when it started. It reads "Friends · since 25 Aug 2026", or names the request it grew out of: "Helping with "Groceries" · since 25 Aug 2026" while that request is still going, "Helped with "Groceries"" once it is finished, or "Started from a help request". This line waits for the friendship details to arrive.
- A small Message button that opens the chat. It appears once the friendship details have arrived.
- The points you have earned with that helper, in gold, like 9/15. Touch the number to open your Trust Score page.
- The seven steps, drawn as a row of circles.
- A switch reading "Let my family see this friendship". Under it the app says "Your family can see this friendship." when it is on, or "Kept private from family. Only you can change this." when it is off. While it is on there is also a button reading Open the family group.
- Take a break in the bottom right corner. There is no End button on this screen.

What an open row shows on the helper's screen

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (5)
text:
- The same step line, "Stage 4 of 7 · Video".
- The same reason line: "Friends · since 25 Aug 2026", or the request you were accepted on, by name.
- The elder's age, written "Age 78", when the app has been told it.
- A small Message button that opens the chat.
- The points you have earned with that elder, in gold, like 9/15. Here it is plain writing, and touching it does nothing.
- Their phone number, with a small telephone picture beside it, once the app has been sent it. The rule is written on your own profile: touch Edit, and under Phone number it says "Only shared after both people reach the Phone Ready trust stage."
- The seven steps, drawn as a row of circles.
- A short list headed "{Name}'s family", when anyone in that elder's family stands behind this friendship. Each person is named with their relationship, and under the name it says either "You can message each other while this friendship stays shared." or "Can see how this friendship is going and may message you." A Message button sits beside anyone whose chat is already open.
- A button reading Open the family group, while the elder is sharing this friendship with their family.
- Take a break and End in the bottom right corner.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (6)
text: Note: The gold number on a row is always your own score with that person, on either screen. The Trust Score page says so in your own words. An elder reads: "Each helper you grow trust with can earn you up to 15 points: 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, 2 for your profile, and 1 for family connected." A helper reads: "Each person you help can earn you up to 15 points: 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, and 3 for your profile."

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (7)
text:
The seven circles are the ladder itself, and they are drawn the same way on both screens. A step you have already climbed is a filled blue circle with a tick. The step you are on now is an empty circle with a blue ring. Steps ahead are empty circles with a grey ring, so you can always count what is left. The seventh circle is different: it holds the Towinly tortoise in a pale blue disc, at every stage. The line joining two circles turns blue once you pass it. Under the circles are three words: "Connected" on the left, "Trusted" on the right in gold, and in the middle, in blue, the one you are about to take, written "Next: Phone". The middle word goes away at the top of the ladder, because there is no next. The same drawing appears on the family screens, so everybody is looking at one picture.

Which button you see, and when

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (8)
text:
The moment | On the elder's screen, My Helpers | On the helper's screen, My Elders
Neither of you has tapped yet | The blue button Start the next step | The line "{Name} starts each trust step. You'll get a tap here to accept."
The elder has tapped and the helper has not accepted | The line "You've started the next step. Waiting for {Name} to accept." | The blue button Accept the next step
Step 7 is reached | A green box: "Fully trusted", and under it "Seven steps, climbed together. The whole ladder is complete." No button. | The same green box, and no button

Note: The elder starts every step, so a helper never sees a Start the next step button anywhere.

Take care: Open a row in the first second after the app starts and the blue Start the next step button may be missing altogether on the elder's screen. The app hides it until it knows where the friendship stands, so that your first tap is not refused. Wait a moment and it appears.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (9)
text:
Both buttons ask before anything moves. The elder's box is headed "Start the next step?" and says "Trust grows only when BOTH of you agree. {Name} will get a tap to accept.", with Not yet and Start underneath. The helper's box is headed "Accept the next step?" and says "{Name} has asked to move one step up. Accepting climbs the ladder for both of you.", with Not yet and Accept. Taking the step from inside the chat brings up the same box with the same words.

When it goes through, a short message appears along the bottom of the screen. If you moved first it reads "Step confirmed. Waiting for {Name} to agree too." If yours was the second yes it reads "You both agreed. One step up the ladder!" and the row gains a circle. When it fails, nothing moves and the message reads "Could not confirm right now. Please try again." If you have not confirmed your email address yet, it reads "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again." instead.

When somebody in the family takes the step for you

1. On the parent's screen, under the friendship, touch Move the next step forward for {parent}.
2. Touch Yes, move it for {parent} to go ahead, or Not now to stop.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (10)
text:
Between those two touches the app asks in place: "Take {parent}'s next step with {first name}? The step counts as theirs." When it goes through, a message along the bottom reads "Step taken for {parent}. {first name} will see you moved it."

Note: Under the button, in gold, the app repeats: "The step counts as {parent}'s. {first name} sees that you took it for them." The button is gone once the ladder is at the top, because there is nothing left to take.

The blue number beside a name

A folded row can carry a small blue circle with a white 1 in it, between the name and the arrow. On the helper's screen it means a step is waiting for you to accept, and looking at the row changes nothing. On the elder's screen it means the helper has accepted and the friendship has climbed. It stays until you start the next step, so it cannot be read away by mistake. At the top of the ladder there is no next step to start, so opening the row is enough to clear it.

On the helper's screen the number goes when you touch Accept inside the box headed "Accept the next step?" and the app has saved the step. Touching the blue Accept the next step button and then Not yet leaves the number where it was.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (11)
text:
Take care: The number on the first button at the bottom of the screen, My Helpers or My Elders, is a wider count than the numbers in the list. It counts people who have anything new for you, and that includes a brand new friendship that has nothing to do with a trust step. So the bottom of the screen can read 2 while only one row in the list wears a blue 1. A person with two new things counts once.

A break, and the way back

Take a break sits in the bottom right corner of the open row on both screens. It asks first, in a box headed "Take a break?". On the elder's screen it names the person: "Trust steps and messages with {Name} pause until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost." On the helper's screen it names nobody: "Trust steps and messages with this elder pause until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost." The buttons are Not now and Take a break. Afterwards a message along the bottom reads "Paused. You can resume any time." and carries Undo. That message and its Undo stay for about six seconds and then go, so decide while it is there.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (12)
text:
The person does not disappear. Their row turns into a small card with their picture, their name, the line "On a break. Trust steps and messages are paused.", and one Resume button. It stays under the heading it was under, so a friend at the top of the ladder stays under Trusted Friends or Trusted Elders. Their chat says the same thing: "You two are on a break. Messages are paused." with Resume under it. Either of you can resume, from either place, and the app answers "Welcome back. Trust steps and messages are on again."

Note: One thing does go quiet during a break. A paused friendship drops off the Trust Score page until it is resumed, so its card and its points are not listed there while the break lasts. Nothing is lost, and it all comes back when either of you touches Resume.

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (13)
text:
Take care: Ending is a different thing from a break, and it cannot be undone. On the helper's screen the open row has End beside Take a break. It asks "End this connection?" and says "You and {Name} will no longer be connected. This cannot be undone.", with Keep it and End. Afterwards the app says "Connection ended." The elder's row has no End button. Either person can also end a friendship from the other person's profile, where the button reads End friendship. That one asks "End this friendship?" and says "You and {Name} will no longer be connected. This cannot be undone.", with Keep friendship and End it.

What each step turns on

Note: Steps 4 and 5, called Video Ready and Social Media, turn nothing on inside the app. They are the agreement itself, written down: a video call, then the other places you can be found. The ladder keeps the record so neither of you has to remember who said what.

The same seven steps, counted as points

heading: For everybody / The Trust Ladder (14)
text:
Nothing on that page moves a friendship. There is no Start the next step and no Accept the next step there. Steps are taken on the row on your home screen, or inside that person's chat, or by a family member the elder has trusted with it. The app offers no control anywhere that lowers a step or skips one.

Note: The five review points are real, and the app tells you plainly where they come from. Near the top of the Trust Score page it says: "Reviews are written on the Towinly website. You cannot leave one from the app yet." One person can write one in the app: a family member, on their parent's behalf. That needs two things at once. The elder must have switched on "Leave a review for you", and the friendship must have reached step 7. With both in place, Leave a review for {parent} appears under that friendship on the parent's screen. Below step 7 the button is not on the screen at all.

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (1)
text:
One number, built out of the friendships you have earned. It is on your profile and on the shield at the top of the screen.

Your Trust Score for an elder. Under the heading comes the scoring line, and the line pointing to the website comes after it. Further down the page, each helper's card carries a Their review row scored out of 5.

Each person you build trust with can add up to 15 points. Where those 15 come from depends on which seat you are in, and the app says so on the page itself.

Your seat | How the 15 points are made
Elder | 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, 2 for your profile, and 1 for family connected
Helper | 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, and 3 for your profile
Family | Your score comes from your profile. Fill it in to earn your first points.

The 7 is the ladder itself, one point for each step. The 5 comes from the review that person writes about you once you reach the top. The rest comes from your own profile.

Every person you have built trust with, and where their 15 points stand.

The tiers

Your total puts you in a tier, and the page tells you how many points to the next one.

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (2)
text:
Points | Tier
0 | New Member
1 | Getting Started
15 | Reliable
45 | Highly Trusted
90 | Community Champion

An elder with any family connected gets one extra point. One point in total, however many family members they add.

Reviews, and where they show

A review is worth 5 of the 15 points a person can earn with you, and it can only be written once a friendship reaches the top of the ladder.

Reviews are written on the Towinly website. You cannot write one from the app yet, and the Trust Score page says so rather than hiding it. The one exception is a family member writing a review for a parent who has allowed it.

A review written about you appears on your own Profile, under the heading What friends say about me, as a row of stars and the words they wrote. Up to three are shown. If nobody has reviewed you, the whole card is missing rather than showing an empty box.

A helper's own Profile, scrolled down to What friends say about me. The stars come first, then the words. No name shows.

Where your points come from, person by person

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (3)
text:
Further down the Trust Score page, each person you have built trust with has their own card. It breaks the 15 points into the four parts and shows how many of each you have: Trust stages out of 7, Their review out of 5, Your profile, and Family for an elder.

Two of Margaret's helpers, and where each of their 15 points stands.

Underneath is Your profile, a checklist of the things that earn the profile points: a profile photo, a short bio, your date of birth, your occupation, your interests and a social link, then phone and identity verification. Each one you complete is ticked.

Who can write a review, and when

A review is a rating out of five stars, with a few words underneath if the writer adds them. Reviews sit at the very top of the trust ladder. The ladder is the seven steps two people climb together, from Just Connected up to Fully Trusted, and a card shows where you are with a line such as Stage 7 of 7. Only when a friendship has reached that seventh step can the two people write a review of each other.

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (4)
text:
- An elder writes about a helper, and a helper writes about an elder. Both are written on the Towinly website, in the boxes described below.
- Before the seventh step there is no review button to press. Towinly does not draw one, so there is nothing to hunt for.
- A review attached to a finished help request can only be written once. Send a second one on the same request and Towinly answers "You've already reviewed this." A review written from a friendship carries no request with it, so that particular answer never appears there.
- When one person has written about you more than once, only their newest review counts toward your points. The older ones stay on your page for anyone to read.

Where a review is written

The app itself has no review form for an elder or a helper. Your Trust Score says so in a line of its own: "Reviews are written on the Towinly website. You cannot leave one from the app yet." A family member does not see that line, because a family member does have a review box in the app. That one is described at the end of this section.

The review boxes on the website

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (5)
text:
There are four, and they are not worded alike. An elder has two: one on a finished help request under Posted Help, opened with the button ★ Leave a Review, and one on a fully trusted friendship under My Helpers, opened with the button Review. A helper has one, on a fully trusted friendship under My Elders, opened with the button Review. Those three all end with Submit Review and Cancel. The fourth is the family member's box, described at the end of this section. It is on the website as well as in the app, in the same words.

The three an elder or a helper uses read like this.

Which box | Heading on the box | Words you can tick | Comment box
Elder, finished help request | Rate your helper | Friendly, Punctual, Respectful, Helpful, Patient | Add a comment (optional)
Elder, friendship | Rate and the helper's name | Punctual, Kind, Trustworthy, Patient, Helpful | Share your experience (optional)
Helper, friendship | Rate and the elder's name | Friendly, Punctual, Respectful, Helpful, Patient | Any comments? (optional)

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (6)
text:
Take care: A safety tick sits on two of those three boxes. The elder's finished help request box has Flag a safety concern. The helper's friendship box has Report a safety concern. The elder's friendship box has no safety tick at all, so an elder who wants one has to use the box on the finished help request. Send a review with the tick on and it shows to everyone as written by "Anonymous", with no name on it.

Before the seventh step, the elder's finished help request says so plainly instead of offering a box: "Helped by" the helper's name, then "You can leave a review once you two are fully trusted friends.", with a button reading Build trust together. With no finished help at all, the Completed list reads "No finished help yet. Completed help shows here so you can leave a review."

After you send one, the finished help request shows the words "Review submitted", and a friendship shows Reviewed where the Review button was. Reload the page and the button comes back, but a second review of the same finished request is refused.

How a review looks in the app

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (7)
text:
Open somebody else's page and their reviews sit under the heading What others say. Every review that person has is listed, newest first. Each one shows a row of gold stars, one star for each star given, then the words if any were written, then the word "by" and the name of whoever wrote it. If your phone reads the screen aloud, it says the whole rating, for example "4 out of 5 stars".

Your own reviews sit on your Profile under a different heading, What friends say about me, and only the three newest are shown. No writer's name appears there.

When somebody reviews an elder or a helper, Updates carries a line reading the writer's name and "wrote you a review", with their words underneath. Tapping that line opens your Profile. A review sent with the safety tick on shows the name "Anonymous" here too. A family member's Updates never carries these lines.

What a review is worth

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (8)
text:
An elder or a helper can earn up to 15 points from each person they grow trust with, and five of those come from that person's review. A helper reads "Each person you help can earn you up to 15 points: 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, and 3 for your profile." An elder reads "Each helper you grow trust with can earn you up to 15 points: 7 for growing trust together, 5 from their review, 2 for your profile, and 1 for family connected." A family member reads something else in the same place: "Your score comes from your profile. Fill it in to earn your first points." Reviews are no part of a family member's score.

On that person's card the row is marked Their review with a number beside it such as 0/5, drawn as five small stars in the page's deep blue that fill in from the left. One star is one point, five stars are five. Only that person's newest review of you is counted. A review you write adds nothing to your own total. It raises theirs.

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (9)
text:
Tip: The stars on Share feedback are a different thing. They sit under Rate the app (optional) on seven rows: Idea, How it looks, Theme, Feeling safe, Ease of Use, How fast it feels and Overall. They rate Towinly itself, and they change nobody's trust score.

A family member writing for a parent

The permission lives on the family member's What I can do tab, under the heading "What I can do for" and the parent's name. Before it is asked for, the line reads "Not on yet. You can ask" the parent's name, then "Reviews unlock when a friendship is fully trusted.", with a button reading Ask and the parent's name. Once asked, the line reads "You asked. Waiting for" the parent's name, "to decide. They answer on their My Family page.", and the word Waiting sits beside it. Once granted, the line reads the parent's name and "lets you do this.", with a green On beside it.

A daughter's view of What I can do for her mother Margaret. The first two powers show On. Leave a review for you, last in the list, has been asked for and shows Waiting.

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (10)
text:
Note: The parent answers on their own My Family page, which has three tabs. The ask arrives on the My family tab under the heading "They're asking you", as a line reading the family member's name and "asks: leave a review for you". Underneath it says "If you say yes:" and then the family member's name and "can rate a helper you fully trust. The review is yours, with" their name "on it as the person who wrote it. It's your choice, and you can turn it off again any time." The two buttons are Yes and Not now.

Note: The parent can also turn this on or off without being asked. The switch is on the Controls tab, under Act for me, named Leave a review for you. Turned off, the words under it read "Off." and the family member's name and "cannot leave a review for you." Turned on, they read the words in the ask above. Act for me shows no switches at all until at least one friendship is shared. Until then it reads "Share a friendship first".

heading: For everybody / Your trust score (11)
text: Above those buttons the app repeats whose review this is: "This is saved as" your parent's name, "review, with your name on it as the person who wrote it." When it saves, a message reads "Review saved for" your parent's name, then the helper's first name and "will see you wrote it.", and the box closes down to one gold line, "Review saved for" your parent's name, "with your name on it." To close the box without sending anything, tap Never mind.

heading: For everybody / Messages (1)
text:
Every conversation you have, sorted by who it is with.

An elder's inbox: the search box, then the headings Helpers, Groups and Family, then one row for each chat carrying a name, a time and one line of the last message.

The Messages button on the bar at the bottom opens your inbox. Conversations are sorted into three groups, and which groups you get depends on your seat: an elder sees Helpers, Groups and Family; a helper sees Elders, Groups and Family; a family member sees Helpers, Groups and Family.

A group you cannot fill yet still appears, empty, with a line saying what would put something in it. That way the app never hides a part of itself from you.

Note: The red number on a group counts people waiting, not messages. Somebody who sent you seven messages counts as one. Towinly counts this way everywhere.

Inside a conversation

A chat with Ethan Cole. Today is printed on its own above the first message, the elder's own message carries 9:12 AM · Sent underneath, and the writing box waits at the bottom.

heading: For everybody / Messages (2)
text:
Messages run oldest at the top and newest at the bottom, with the day marked between them. Under your own messages the app says "Sent" and then "Seen". A message that failed stays on screen saying "Didn't send. Tap to try again.", and tapping it tries again.

Type in the box at the bottom and tap the round send button. It stays greyed out until there is something to send.

When there is no box to type in

A brand new friendship cannot message yet. Instead of an empty box the app explains: "You're connected. Messages unlock at the next trust step." Underneath is the one thing you can do, which depends on your seat. An elder gets Start the next step. A helper gets Accept the next step once the elder has started one, and otherwise a line saying the elder starts each step.

A paused friendship says "You two are on a break. Messages are paused." with a Resume button. Either of you can resume.

Group chats

When an elder shares a friendship with their family, a small group chat opens on it. It is marked "Group chat. Everyone sharing it reads along", so nobody is ever in it without knowing.

Finding one chat among many

heading: For everybody / Messages (3)
text:
A search box sits above your chats. It appears once you have at least one chat, and the word inside it before you type is Search. Type a few letters of a name and the list narrows while you type. Capital letters and accents make no difference, so typing jose finds José. The box searches only the heading you have open, so a name filed under Family stays hidden while Helpers is on screen. When nothing matches, the app says No matches for, then your words in quotation marks, then a full stop. Clear the box to bring every chat back. To change heading, tap it, or swipe the list sideways with your finger. The inbox opens on the first heading that has a chat in it.

Under Helpers, Elders and Family, each row is one person. It starts with a round picture of them. If they have added a photo you see the photo. If they have not, you see the first letters of their name on a plain grey circle, so EC stands for Ethan Cole. That is normal and nothing is broken. Beside the name, on the right, is how long ago the last message was written. A chat where neither of you has written yet shows no time at all.

heading: For everybody / Messages (4)
text:
Under the name is one line. It shows the last message in that chat, cut short with a … if it runs long. If nobody has written yet, that line reads Say hello. On a helper's screen only, a row for an elder's family member reads whose family they are instead, such as Margaret's family. A row with messages you have not read sits in darker, heavier type with a number on the right, and that number counts the messages that one person sent you.

Rows under Groups are built differently. A group row carries a blue circle with a people mark in it, the name of the group, and one fixed line underneath: "Group chat. Everyone sharing it reads along". A group row never shows a time and never shows a number.

Note: The number beside a heading such as Helpers or Family counts PEOPLE waiting, not messages. A heading reading 4 means four people have written to you, however many messages each of them sent. Groups never carries a number.

What the time says | What it means
now | In the last minute.
5m | Five minutes ago.
3h | Three hours ago.
2d | Two days ago.
Aug 12 | A week or more ago, so the date is shown instead.

The headings across the top, and what each says while empty

heading: For everybody / Messages (5)
text:
Nobody sees all four headings. You get three, and which three depends on whether you joined as an elder, a helper or a family member. An elder never sees Elders. A helper never sees Helpers. A heading with no chats in it stays on screen and explains itself.

Heading | Who sees it | What it says while empty | Button under it
Helpers | Elders and family members | No chats with helpers yet. A chat opens when someone offers to help, or when you become friends. | Find friends
Elders | Helpers | No chats with elders yet. A chat opens when you offer to help with a request. | Offer help
Groups | Everyone | No group chats yet. When a friendship is shared with family, its updates will show here. | None
Family | Everyone | No family chats yet. When a family member joins you here, your chat with them will show up. | None

Blocking hides a person from your one to one chats. Their row is taken out of Helpers, Elders and Family and does not come back. A family member's Groups list is built from their parents' shared friendships instead, so a group named after a helper a family member has blocked can still sit there.

An empty inbox, and one that will not load

heading: For everybody / Messages (6)
text:
Before anything at all has happened there are no headings and no search box. The screen reads "No conversations yet", then "Chats open up once you're friends with someone, or when help is offered on a request." An elder gets Ask Help under that, a helper gets Offer Help, and both also get Find friends. A family member gets no button here.

A list that fails to load says so. The inbox reads "We couldn't load your conversations right now. Please check your connection and try again." with a Try again button. The Groups heading has its own version of that line: "We couldn't load your group chats right now. Please check your connection and try again." Neither one is ever dressed up as an empty inbox. You can also pull the list down with your finger to fetch everything again.

Inside a chat

heading: For everybody / Messages (7)
text:
At the top of a one to one chat is a back arrow, then the other person's picture and name. Tapping the name opens their profile. The messages fill the screen, newest at the bottom. Your own messages sit on the right in a rounded pale blue shape, and theirs sit on the left in a pale grey one. Each of those shapes is called a bubble in the rest of this chapter. At the very bottom is the writing box, which reads Write a message… until you type. The round send button beside it is grey while the box is empty and turns blue once there are words in it.

The marks under your messages

- "Sending…" while the message is on its way.
- "9:12 AM · Sent" once Towinly has it.
- "9:12 AM · Seen" once the other person has opened the chat.
- "Didn't send. Tap to try again." in red when it failed.
- A message from the other person shows the time on its own, with no mark after it.

heading: For everybody / Messages (8)
text:
The day is printed on its own, in the middle of the screen, above the first message of that day. Nothing is drawn around it. It says Today or Yesterday, and for anything older it writes the day out in full, such as Saturday, August 23. One is always printed above the oldest message on screen, and another appears wherever the day changes.

While you are sitting in a chat, Towinly checks for new messages every five seconds, so a reply lands without you doing anything. Leaving the chat stops that checking. Opening a chat also marks that person's messages as read. The number on their row goes, and so do the numbers on the heading above and on Messages at the bottom of the screen.

A message that did not send

The message stays where you put it. Its bubble keeps your words and reads "Didn't send. Tap to try again." in red underneath. A short note also appears near the bottom of the screen saying "Message didn't send. Tap the message to try again." and goes away after a few seconds. If your email address is still unverified, that note reads "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again." instead.

heading: For everybody / Messages (9)
text:
1. Find the bubble marked "Didn't send. Tap to try again."
2. Tap that bubble.
3. Watch the words under it change to "Sending…".
4. When it goes through, the red line is replaced by the time and the word Sent.

Take care: Anything you have typed since is never written over. If you leave the chat with messages still unsent, Towinly puts their words back into the writing box, oldest first, above anything you had already typed. Nothing you wrote is thrown away. Whatever sits in a writing box is kept while the app is open and cleared when you log out.

Words Towinly will not send

When you tap send, Towinly reads the message before it leaves your phone. If it holds a word Towinly will not carry, a red line appears just above the writing box with a small round warning mark beside it. It says Please take out, then the word itself in quotation marks, then "Towinly is read by older people who are trusting us with their homes." Your message stays in the box so you can change the word, and the red line goes as soon as you edit it. The check looks at whole words, so ordinary words and place names that happen to contain one of them are left alone.

Locked, waiting and paused, word for word

heading: For everybody / Messages (10)
text:
A brand new friendship between an elder and a helper cannot carry messages until the two of you have taken the first trust step together. While that is true, a short notice stands where the writing box would be. Its first line is always "You're connected. Messages unlock at the next trust step." What sits under it depends on your seat and on whose turn it is. Family chats and group chats are never locked this way.

1. Tap Start the next step at the bottom of the chat.
2. Read the question "Start the next step?" and the line under it: "Trust grows only when BOTH of you agree. Ethan Cole will get a tap to accept."
3. Tap Start to go ahead, or Not yet to leave things as they are.
4. Wait while the button reads "Confirming…".

Take care: Now and then a chat locks while you are still looking at the old screen. The message is refused and Towinly says "Your trust level is too low to message yet. Take the next trust step together first." Your words go back into the writing box, and the trust notice takes the place of the box.

The group chat on a shared friendship

heading: For everybody / Messages (11)
text: The row in the inbox is named after the two people in the friendship. It reads "You & Ethan Cole" from your own seat and "Margaret & Ethan Cole" from the family's seat, with "Group chat. Everyone sharing it reads along" under it. Inside, the top of the screen carries the line "Family group. Everyone here reads along", and every message that is not yours carries the name of whoever wrote it.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (1)
text:
Search for somebody new, answer invitations, and see who has not answered yours.

An elder's Find New Helpers list. The three parts sit under the heading, then the location box, then the five distance buttons, then the people. On the right of each name is Connect for someone you have not asked, or the word Friends for someone you are already connected to.

Three parts across the top: Find New Helpers or Find New Elders, depending on your seat, then New Invites and Requested, each with a count.

Looking for somebody

The find list shows people near you. A row of distances sits at the top, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 km, and you tap the one you want. Each person's row shows their photo, name, age, their trust score in gold or the words "New here", and how far away they are.

The small button on the right tells you where you stand with that person: Connect to ask, Requested if you already have, Accept if they asked you first, or Friends if you are already connected.

1. Choose a distance.
2. Find somebody, and tap Connect on their row.
3. Towinly asks "Send a friend request?" and says they will be asked to connect with you.
4. Tap Send request, or Not now to think about it.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (2)
text:
Take care: A request cannot be taken back once sent. Towinly asks you to confirm for that reason. The Requested tab shows what you are waiting on, with no cancel button, because there is no way to cancel one.

Answering an invitation

New Invites holds anyone who asked to connect with you, along with the message they sent. Tap Accept and Towinly says "You are now friends!". Tap Decline and it asks first, and tells you that they will be told, and that they can invite you again later.

About your location

Towinly asks before using it, and explains what it keeps: a rounded position, about a two kilometre area, so people see roughly how far away you are instead of the town you typed when you joined. It never saves your address, and never looks while the app is closed. Not now is always there, and the screen works without it.

The three parts, and the numbers beside them

heading: For everybody / Finding people (3)
text:
The screen is headed Add Friends and is split into three parts you can move between. The first is Find New Helpers on an elder's phone, or Find New Elders on a helper's. The other two are New Invites and Requested. Only those last two carry a number, and the number shows even when it is 0. A 1 beside New Invites means one person has asked to connect with you. A 1 beside Requested means one person is holding a request from you and has not answered yet. The first part carries no number at all. You move between the three by tapping one, or by dragging the list sideways with your finger. The distance buttons and the location box belong to the first part alone.

How the five distances work

Above the people is a line reading Showing helpers within on an elder's screen, or Showing elders within on a helper's. Under it sit five buttons: 5 km, 10 km, 25 km, 50 km and 100 km. 25 km is already chosen when the screen opens, and the one in use is filled pale blue. Each tap sends that distance to Towinly and asks for a fresh list. The people already on screen stay put while the answer comes back, so nothing blinks under your thumb.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (4)
text:
The line under a name holds two things, with a dot between them. First the trust score in deep green, printed as a number and the word trust, like "3 trust". When a person has no points yet, that place reads New here instead. Then how far away they are. One kilometre or more reads as a whole number, like "3 km away". Anything closer reads "in your area". Towinly rounds every position onto a grid of squares roughly two kilometres wide, so two people inside the same square work out as no distance apart, and "in your area" is the honest way to say that.

Note: A helper who has no position of their own does still appear on an elder's list. Their line reads "in your area", and they stay in the list at every distance setting.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (5)
text:
What is on the right of the name | What it means
Connect | You have not asked this person yet. Tapping it opens a question first, so a mis-tap sends nothing.
Sending… | Your request is on its way. Only the person you tapped changes to this word.
Requested | You have already asked. It is grey, and tapping it sends nothing. The tap opens that person's page instead.
Accept | They asked you first. Tapping it says yes at once, with no question in between.
Accepting… | An answer is on its way. Every line that was showing Accept changes to this word at the same moment, so it does not tell you which person you tapped.
Friends | You are already friends. The word Friends shows in green, and tapping it opens their page.

Note: Only one request or one answer can be on its way at a time. While one is going, the small buttons on all the other people send nothing. Tapping one opens that person's page. Tapping a person's name or photo does the same, so you can read about them before you ask.

Sending a friend request

heading: For everybody / Finding people (6)
text:
1. Tap Find New Helpers at the top, or Find New Elders if you are a helper.
2. Find the person you want and tap Connect on the right of their name.
3. Read the question that opens. It is headed "Send a friend request?" and under it says their name, then "will be asked to connect with you."
4. Tap Send request to send it. Tap Not now, or tap the dimmed area around the question, to send nothing at all.
5. Watch the button read Sending… and then settle on Requested. A short message says "Friend request sent!" and clears itself after about four seconds.

That person now also appears under Requested, in a box saying "Waiting for … to accept. They'll see your request in their invites.", with their name in the gap. The box carries a grey Requested button. Tapping it opens their page, the same as tapping their name. There is no cancel button of any kind.

Take care: A sent request cannot be withdrawn, from this screen or from anywhere else in Towinly.

When a request will not send

If Towinly refuses the request, a short message says why in its own words. Here are some of the sentences you may meet.

Accepting an invite

heading: For everybody / Finding people (7)
text:
1. Tap New Invites at the top.
2. Tap Accept under the person's name. There is no question to confirm, so the answer goes the moment you tap.
3. Wait while a small circle spins beside the word Accept. The buttons on every other invite stop working until it lands.
4. Read the message that says "You are now friends!" Their box then leaves the list.

Note: If somebody asked you first, they also show on the find list with Accept in place of Connect. Tapping it there sends the same answer.

Take care: Accepting can be refused too, and the words are the same for every reason: "Could not respond right now. Please try again." They never carry Towinly's own reason. The two limits are checked again at the moment you accept, 10 friendships for an elder and 20 for a helper, so a full list is one thing those words can mean. If they keep coming back, open a friend's page, tap End friendship, then accept again.

Declining an invite

Take care: Towinly sends the other person no message about a decline. Their request leaves their Requested list, with no word of any kind.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (8)
text:
Take care: A declined invite cannot be brought back. It leaves New Invites for good and there is no screen in the app that shows it again. The person you declined cannot ask you a second time either: their Connect on your name answers "A duplicate value already exists." If you change your mind, send them a request yourself from Find New Helpers or Find New Elders.

Note: If your answer cannot go through, the message reads "Could not respond right now. Please try again." and the invite stays where it was.

Empty lists, and lists that failed to load

When nobody is near enough, the find list says "Nobody new within 25 km right now. Try a wider distance, or check back soon.", with whichever distance you chose in place of the 25. An empty New Invites says "No new invites. When someone asks to connect, they appear here." An empty Requested says "No requests waiting. People you ask to connect with appear here."

heading: For everybody / Finding people (9)
text:
A list that failed to load is given different words, so a dropped connection is never mistaken for an empty list. It says "We couldn't load people near you right now. Please check your connection and try again.", with a Try again button under it. The same sentence names "your invites" or "your requests" on the other two parts. Dragging any of the three lists down with your finger loads all three again.

The location box, word for word

Towinly asks you before your phone asks you. The box at the top of the find list is headed "See who is nearby" and says: "Towinly can use your location to show how far away each person is, and to show only people within the distance you choose. We save a rounded position, about a two kilometre area, never your address. Never while the app is closed." Under it are a blue Use my location button, which reads Just a moment… while it works, and a quieter Not now underneath. Tapping Use my location is what brings up your phone's own permission question. Tapping Not now hides the box until you leave this screen and come back.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (10)
text:
What gets saved is a rounded reading. Your phone works out where it is, then Towinly rounds that reading onto a grid of squares about two kilometres across before it leaves the phone. Only those rounded numbers are sent to your Towinly account. Your street address is never saved, and Towinly never reads your position while the app is shut. Once you have said yes, if the saved reading is more than a day old, Towinly reads the phone again when you open a screen that needs it, once, without asking you anything.

Take care: On an iPhone your phone asks this question once and once only. If you tap Don't Allow there, Towinly can never ask again from inside the app. The box then reads "Location is turned off for Towinly" and tells you: "To show distances again, open Settings on your phone, find Towinly, and turn Location on. Everyone below still shows without it." It carries no button, because only your phone settings can change it now.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (11)
text:
If your phone lets the question be asked more than once, saying no gives you softer words. The box is headed "Distances are hidden" and says: "Without your location we cannot tell you how far away anyone is. You can still see everyone below, and you can turn this on whenever you like." Use my location is still there to change your mind, and Not now is gone. Those words last while you stay on the screen. Come back to it later and the box asks again in its first words.

If location is switched off for the whole phone, the box reads "Location is turned off on this phone" and says: "Turn Location on in your phone settings and Towinly can show how far away each person is. Everyone below still shows without it." It carries no button either.

Note: Once your location is working, the box disappears from this screen. New Invites and Requested work on both phones whether or not Towinly has a position for you.

heading: For everybody / Finding people (12)
text: Take care: The find list is the part that differs. On an elder's phone nothing is locked behind a position: every helper still shows, and the only thing you lose is the distance under each name. On a helper's phone the list of elders cannot be built without one, so a helper who has neither tapped Use my location nor typed a place in the My town or city box on Edit Profile sees the "couldn't load" words in place of people.

heading: For everybody / Updates (1)
text:
Everything new for you, in one list, with nothing disappearing behind your back.

An elder's Updates list. The two offers come first, each naming the request in quotation marks. New friendships, a friend request and waiting messages follow below them.

The bell at the top right of your home screen opens Updates. It gathers everything: friend requests, new friendships, offers on your requests, an elder saying yes to your offer, reviews written about you, alerts about a parent, and anyone asking you to hold a key.

Note: Opening this screen does not clear it. A row keeps its blue background, and the bell keeps counting it, until you tap that particular row. Nothing vanishes because you glanced at the list.

When there is nothing, the screen says "Nothing new right now." and tells you what would appear here. If Towinly cannot reach the internet it says that instead, rather than pretending the list is empty.

Alerts on your phone

Towinly can put a short line on your phone when something happens. This guide calls that line an alert. An alert shows a person's name and one short sentence. Nothing else is shown on it.

heading: For everybody / Updates (2)
text:
Four things send an alert in this version. Nothing else does. When the app is closed, an alert arrives with your phone's usual notification sound.

What happened | What the phone shows | What tapping it opens
Somebody wrote to you in a conversation | Their name, then "sent you a message." | That conversation
Somebody wrote on a shared updates thread you are on | Their name, then "sent you a message." | That updates thread
Somebody offered to help with a request you posted | Their name, then "offered to help with your request." | Your Posted Help list
Somebody accepted your offer to help | Their name, then "accepted your offer to help." | My offers & jobs

A shared updates thread belongs to a friendship that has been shared with family. Inside Messages it sits under the heading Groups. There is more about it further down.

The offer alert goes to the elder who posted the request, even when a family member looks after that request for them. The acceptance alert carries the elder's name, even when a family member pressed accept on the elder's behalf. The connection made there belongs to the elder, and the alert says so.

heading: For everybody / Updates (3)
text:
Take care: The words of a message are never on an alert. The title of your help request is never on one either. Somebody who picks up your locked phone sees that a named person wrote to you, and nothing about what was said or what you asked for. That is on purpose: a lock screen is not a private place. Open the app to read it.

An alert only goes out after the action behind it is safely saved. A message that fails to send never rings anyone's phone.

The name on an alert is checked first

The name on an alert is the name that person chose for themselves, so Towinly checks it before your lock screen shows it. Four things can happen to it.

- A name that is blank or missing shows as "Someone".
- A name that looks like a web address shows as "Someone". A full address counts, and so does a plain word with a dot and an ending like .com or .co in it.
- A name holding seven digits or more shows as "Someone". Every digit anywhere in the name is counted together, so "Anna 1948 Delhi 2011" has eight digits and shows as "Someone".
- A name longer than 40 characters is shortened to fit, and ends with three dots.

heading: For everybody / Updates (4)
text:
Note: This is why the rule exists. A lock screen shows the name under Towinly's own name, with no way to report it and nothing around it. Somebody who called themselves "CALL 1 900 555 0123 to claim your refund" would otherwise be putting that line on an elder's lock screen. The check runs on the alert only. Inside the app you see the name as it was written.

Who gets a message alert

An elder and a helper in a conversation each get an alert when the other one writes. Family members are alerted too, on the conversations they sit in themselves: the private chat with their parent, and their chat with a helper. If your parent writes to you, your phone tells you.

A shared updates thread works differently. Family members can read it, and they get no alert from it. When the elder or the helper writes on it, the other one gets an alert. When a family member writes on it, the elder and the helper both get an alert, and it carries the family member's name.

Take care: So a family member who is not in your one to one chat can still light up your phone. If you are an elder or a helper on a shared friendship, an alert may carry the name of your friend's daughter or son.

heading: For everybody / Updates (5)
text:
While the app is already open

A new chat message stays quiet while Towinly is open in front of you. The count on Messages already says it, and a line across the top about the very chat you are reading would only repeat the screen.

The number on the Towinly icon

The number on the Towinly icon on your home screen counts conversations with something unread, so it counts people. Four helpers who wrote to you read as 4, however many messages they sent between them. It falls as you read, and it clears when you log out. Shared updates threads are left out of it.

The counts on the headings inside Messages count people the same way. Groups is the exception. Group threads carry no count, so that heading never shows a number, however many messages are waiting inside it.

An elder's Messages inbox. The headings run Helpers 4, then Groups, then Family 1. The numbers count people waiting. Groups carries no number.

Note: A family member looking for their parent's shared friendship thread finds it under Groups. On a family member's phone, the Family heading holds two things: the private chat with their parent, and their chat with a helper.

Alerts and the Updates list are two different things

heading: For everybody / Updates (6)
text:
The Updates list is inside the app. On your first tab, the bell in the top right corner has the word Updates under it. Tap the bell. Most of what appears there never touched your phone as an alert.

An alert on your phone | The Updates list
Four things only: a message, a message on a shared updates thread, an offer on your request, your offer accepted | Many kinds, listed below
Sent to your phone by Towinly's computers | Put together by the app each time you look
Gone once you clear it off the phone | Stays new until you tap that row
Needs your permission, and can be switched off in the phone's settings | Always there, whatever you answered

What the Updates list holds
