Not every row reaches every reader. What you see depends on the kind of account you signed up with.

Note: A family account never sees a review row. An elder account and a helper account never see an alert about a parent.

heading: For everybody / Updates (7)
text:
Alerts about a parent cover an SOS, a first meeting, a quiet spell with no activity, a keyholder being asked, a Sealed box being set up, and a Sealed box being opened soon after a password change. They sit in the list and make no sound, so a family member should look at the bell now and then, even on a quiet day.

An Updates row names more than an alert does. An offer row names the request in quotation marks, which the alert on your phone never does. A message row names the person, and the number of messages when more than one is waiting.

Note: Your first tab is named My Helpers on an elder's phone, My Elders on a helper's phone, and My Parents on a family member's phone.

Tip: A row stays marked new until you tap that row. Opening Updates and scrolling past does not clear anything, so nothing quietly disappears while you are reading.

Note: Family links never appear as friend requests or new friendships in Updates. Those two rows cover friendships only.

More than one phone

heading: For everybody / Updates (8)
text:
Every phone signs itself up on its own. Sign in on a second phone and both ring. Log out tells Towinly to stop ringing that one phone and leaves your other phones alone. If that phone has no internet at the moment you log out, the app finishes the job the next time it starts.

Take care: An account can hold ten phones at once. Sign in on an eleventh and the phone that went longest without opening Towinly is dropped, and goes quiet. Sign in on it again to bring it back.

Permission, and what Towinly cannot change

Your phone asks for permission after you sign in on an iPhone. The box that appears belongs to the phone and uses the phone's own words, so Towinly has no say in what it says. You answer it there.

Towinly asks the phone again each time you sign in, and the phone decides whether to show you the box. Once you have said no, the phone stops allowing the question, so it does not come back. To change your mind, open your phone's own settings, find Towinly, and turn notifications on there.

Towinly has no notification settings of its own. There is no way inside the app to turn one kind off, set quiet hours, or choose the sound. Your phone's own settings hold all of that.

heading: For everybody / Updates (9)
text: Note: These alerts go to iPhones in this version. Android phones do not receive them yet. Towinly opened in a web browser never rings and never puts a number on an icon. The Updates list works everywhere, including in a browser.

heading: For everybody / Peekaboo
text:
A quiet minute with the tortoise. A small matching game, and nothing else.

Six pairs to find, and a timer. A pair that matches stays open.

Open it from Profile, then Peekaboo, or from the Play button under your daily check-in. Tap two cells on the shell. A pair that matches stays open. Find all six pairs before the clock runs out.

There is a Pause button, and Skip to Home leaves at any time. The game runs on your phone alone. It changes nothing about your account, your trust score, or what anybody else sees.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (1)
text:
Who you are on Towinly, and every setting the app has.

The top of Profile: the photo, the name, the town, the Edit button, and the three numbers marked trust, friends and day streak. Below them are the rows that lead to the rest of your places and your settings.

The last button on the bar at the bottom is Profile. At the top are your photo, your name, your town, and an Edit button. Under those, three numbers: your trust score, how many friends you have, and your day streak.

Editing your details

Tap Edit. You can change your photo, your full name, your date of birth, the languages you speak, how to reach you, and your town or city. Only your age is shown to other people, never your date of birth. Your phone number is only shared once you and the other person both reach the Phone Ready step.

The top of Edit Profile: Change photo, then the About you section with Full name, Date of birth, the About you lines, Occupation and Sex (optional), with Save Changes and Cancel held at the bottom.

Everything on the Profile screen

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (2)
text:
The rows differ a little by seat. An elder sees Daily check-in, My Family and My boxes. A helper sees My offers & jobs and Daily check-in. A family member sees none of those four.

Row | What it opens
Trust Score | Your score, and every person who built it
Peekaboo | The matching game
Guide | Towinly's own explanation of how it works
Get help | How to write to a real person at Towinly
Night mode | A switch. Dark screen, off unless you turn it on
Vibration feedback | A switch for the small buzz when you tap things
Emergency contacts | The people Towinly can call and text for you
Change password | Your current password, then a new one twice
Share feedback | Tell Towinly what helped and what got in your way
Blocked people | Anyone you have blocked, and how to undo it
Privacy policy | What Towinly does with your information
Terms of service | The rules of using Towinly
Account and data | A copy of your data, or deleting your account

Further down Profile: Change password, Share feedback, Blocked people, Privacy policy, Terms of service, then the folded Account and data, with Log out last of all.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (3)
text:
Note: Night mode never turns itself on because your phone did. It stays off until you ask for it. Log out is always the very last thing on the page.

The three numbers under your name

The line under your name is the town saved on your account. If no town is saved, that line shows the word for your seat instead: Elder, Helper, Elder & Helper, or Family member.

The number | What it counts
trust | Your trust score, rounded to a whole number. The same score the Trust Score page sets out.
friends | People where you both said yes. A request still waiting for an answer is not counted.
day streak | Days in a row you have done your daily check-in.

The trust number, and the word trust under it, are written in gold. The other two use the app's ordinary text colour: dark on the light screen, and pale on the dark screen if you have turned night mode on. Towinly keeps these numbers for half a minute after fetching them, so opening Profile again inside that half minute shows you the stored ones without asking again. Pull the screen down with your finger whenever you want them fetched fresh.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (4)
text:
Note: A short dash in place of a number means Towinly could not fetch it. The trust number and the day streak also show that dash for the moment while they are still being fetched. The friends number does not: for that moment it shows 0. So a 0 beside friends that turns into a real number a second after you open Profile is only the fetching catching up.

Further down the same screen, below the settings rows and above Account and data, a card called What friends say about me appears once somebody has reviewed you. It shows the three newest, as gold stars with their words underneath. A review with stars and no words shows the stars alone. If nobody has reviewed you, that card is not on the screen at all.

What friends say about me sitting between the settings rows and Account and data, with five stars and the reviewer's words. This one is a helper's screen.

The rows on Profile, and where each one goes

Account and data, and logging out

Account and data is one row near the bottom with nothing under it until you tap it. Tapping it unfolds two buttons, so that Delete my account is never sitting in the open where a wrong tap can reach it. Tap the row again to fold it away.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (5)
text:
1. Tap Account and data near the bottom of Profile.
2. Tap Send me a copy of my data to have your copy made.
3. In a web browser, look in your downloads. The file saves itself there and there is nothing more to do.
4. On a phone, pick where to send it when your phone offers you its sharing choices.

Note: In a web browser the file is called "Towinly - my information.txt", and Towinly says "Saved. Your copy of your information is in your downloads." On a phone the writing itself goes out through your phone's own sharing choices, and Towinly says "Your copy is ready. Choose where to keep it." If you close those choices without sending it anywhere, Towinly says nothing, because nothing was kept. If the copy cannot be made at all it says "We could not make your copy. Please try again."

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (6)
text:
Take care: Delete my account asks you twice. First "Delete your account?" with the words "This permanently removes your profile, friendships, messages, and requests. It cannot be undone.", and the two answers Keep my account and Delete my account. Then "Are you absolutely sure?" with "There is no way back after this.", and the answers Cancel and Delete forever. Nothing is removed until you answer the second one. When it is done Towinly says "Your account has been deleted." and signs you out. If it cannot be done it says "Could not delete the account right now. Please try again."

Log out is the last thing on the page, below Account and data. It asks first: "Log out?" with the words "You will need your username and password to get back in. If you are not sure you have them, stay logged in." The two answers are Stay logged in and Log out.

The question Log out asks before it does anything, with Stay logged in on the left and Log out on the right.

Night mode and Vibration feedback

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (7)
text:
Night mode is a switch on the right of its row. Turn it on and the whole app changes to a dark screen with pale writing. Towinly remembers your choice and opens that way next time. It never turns itself on because your phone went dark in the evening, and it never follows your phone's own light or dark setting. In the store apps this switch is the only thing that changes it, and it starts off.

Editing your profile, box by box

1. Tap Edit beside your name at the top of Profile. The page is headed Edit Profile.
2. Tap Change photo under the round picture.
3. Say yes if your phone asks Towinly to see your photos.
4. Choose a photo. Your phone lets you move and trim it first.
5. Wait while the button reads Uploading…. Towinly then says "Photo updated."

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (8)
text: Take care: Three things are sent the moment you do them: your photo, your ID, and your position if you press Use my location. Everything else on this screen waits for Save Changes. If you say no to the photo request, the message is "Towinly needs photo access. You can allow it in Settings." If your photos will not open at all it says "Could not open your photos. Please try again." If the sending itself fails, it says "Could not upload the photo. Please try again.", unless your email address has not been confirmed yet, in which case it says "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again."

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (9)
text: The first section is called About you. Full name is the name every other member sees. Date of birth takes any clear way of writing it, and the words under the box say "Any way you like: 1953-05-14 or 14 May 1953. Only your age shows to others." Towinly works your age out from it. There is a second box also called About you, the few lines a helper reads before deciding to connect, and under it: "Shown to helpers before you connect." Occupation asks "What you did or still do." on an elder's screen and "What you do or study." on a helper's. Sex (optional) gives you Male, Female and Other. Tap the one you are. Tap the same one again to leave the question blank.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (10)
text:
- A date written two ways at once, like 04/05/1953, is refused: "That date reads two ways. Please write the month, like 14 May 1953."
- A month word Towinly does not recognise, usually a slip of the finger: "We couldn't read the month. Try like 14 May 1953."
- A date Towinly cannot read at all: "We couldn't read that date. Try like 1953-05-14 or 14 May 1953."
- A day that does not exist, like 31 April: "That date does not exist. Please check it."
- A rude word in your About you lines stops the save and names the word: "Please take out …. Towinly is read by older people who are trusting us with their homes."
- All of these appear under the box itself when you tap Save Changes, never as a message across the screen.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (11)
text:
The next section is What you enjoy if you are an elder, and How you help if you are a helper. My interests, or What I can help with on a helper's screen, takes one thing at a time, and the words underneath say: Type one, like "gardening", then press return. Tap a pill to remove it. A pill is the small rounded box each thing you type turns into, with a little cross in it. A typed comma does the same job as return, and moving on to the next box adds what you have typed too. Helpers get a second box, My hobbies, with "Things you love doing. One at a time, press return after each." Elders answer What I'm looking for with one choice out of Friendship, Help with things and Both. That one cannot be left empty. Languages I speak works like the interests box, and says "One language at a time, press return after each."

Note: If you joined as both an elder and a helper, this screen gives you the elder wording throughout: What you enjoy, My interests and What I'm looking for. The helper wording is for accounts that joined as a helper only.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (12)
text:
How to reach you holds the rest. My town or city carries the line "Used only to match you with people nearby." Phone number carries "Only shared after both people reach the Phone Ready trust stage." Facebook link (optional) and Instagram link (optional) are the last two boxes, and both can stay empty.

On a phone, a card can appear under My town or city offering to use the phone itself instead of the town you type. In a web browser that card is never there, and the town you type is the only way Towinly knows where you are. What the card says depends on what your phone has already been told about location.

Note: Two of the five cards carry Towinly's promise about what is kept, word for word: "We save a rounded position, about a two kilometre area, never your address. Never while the app is closed." They are the card that asks you for the first time, and the card you see once a position has been saved. The other three do not repeat it.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (13)
text:
What the card says | What it offers
Use your phone instead of a typed town | Use my location, with Not now under it. This is the card before you have answered anything.
Your position comes from the town you type | Use my location again, with Not now under it. This is what you see after saying no to your phone's own question.
Location is turned off for Towinly | No Use my location button, because only your phone settings can change this now. It tells you to open Settings on your phone, find Towinly, and turn Location on. Not now is still under it.
Location is turned off on this phone | No Use my location button. It tells you to turn Location on in your phone settings. Not now is still under it.
Your position comes from your phone | Update my location, and no Not now. This is what you see once a position has been saved.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (14)
text:
Take care: Use my location saves at once. It does not wait for Save Changes. Towinly works out the town from the rounded position and writes it into the My town or city box for you, so the box may change under your eyes. While it is working the button reads Just a moment…. Tapping Not now hides the card and says nothing. Your typed town keeps working exactly as before, and the card comes back the next time you open Edit Profile.

Elders get one more section under that, called My Family. It reads "Link your family so they can see you're safe. They only see the friendships you choose to share, and you can remove anyone at any time." and offers Manage My Family, which takes you to the family pages. Nothing is managed on the edit screen itself.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (15)
text:
Save Changes is fixed to the bottom of the screen, with Cancel under it. Tap Save Changes and it reads Saving…, then Towinly says "Profile saved." and takes you back. If it cannot save, it says "Could not save right now. Please try again." and everything you typed stays on the screen. If your email address has not been confirmed yet, the message is "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again." Cancel leaves at once when you changed nothing. When you did change something it asks "Discard your changes?" with "Nothing you typed here will be saved.", and you choose Keep editing or Discard changes.

Changing your password

1. Open Profile and tap Change password. The page is headed "Choose a new password".
2. Type the password you use now into Current password.
3. Type the new one into New password (at least 8 characters).
4. Type that same new one again into Re-enter new password.
5. Tap Update password. It reads Saving… while it works.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (16)
text:
Note: Each of the three boxes has a small eye button on the right. Tap it to see what you typed, and tap it again to hide it. A new password under 8 letters is refused with "New password must be at least 8 characters" under the second box. Two that do not match are refused with "Passwords do not match" under the third.

The other refusals come back from Towinly's machines, and every one of them appears under Current password, whichever box actually caused it. Read the words, not the place they are sitting in.

Take care: When it works, Towinly says "Password updated." and takes you back to Profile. Within about half a minute you are signed out and sent to the log in screen, which says "For your safety, you were logged out after a period of inactivity. Please log in again." This is meant to happen. Changing a password ends every signed-in session, on this phone and on any other, so that anyone who got into your account is locked out. Have your new password to hand before you tap Update password, because you will need it straight away.

heading: For everybody / Your profile and settings (17)
text: Take care: The Sealed box is on the elder's screen, under My boxes. If you keep anything in it, change your password only when you can wait a week. For seven days afterwards nothing in the box will open. It says "You changed your password recently. For your safety your Sealed box stays shut until", then the date it opens again, then "If that was not you, tell us straight away." That week is there so that somebody who took over your email cannot change your password and read your box the same day. Open anything you need out of the box first.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (1)
text:
Blocking, reporting, and the people Towinly can reach for you.

Where the safety buttons are

Inside a conversation, the picture and name at the top open that person's page.

Blocking somebody

Block this person asks first. The question names the person, so for a friend called Helen it reads "Block Helen?". Under it: "You won't see their help requests or messages anymore, and any friendship ends. It follows you to every phone you sign in on." It then says you can change your mind later in Profile, Blocked people. The two buttons are Cancel and Block. Tapping the dimmed area behind the question does the same as Cancel. While the block is saving, the button reads "Blocking…".

Note: The hiding starts on this phone the moment you tap Block. If the phone has no signal, Towinly sends the block up to your account when the signal comes back. Blocking somebody who is not your friend therefore reads the same with or without signal. Blocking a friend needs the network to end the friendship, so with no signal that one shows the second sentence and its Try again button.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (2)
text:
Take care: Report first, then block. After a block, that person's page holds only the words "You've blocked Helen", the line "You won't see their help requests or messages. If this was a mistake, you can undo it." and an Unblock button. Report this person is no longer on it. You can still write to Towinly at any time through Profile, Get help.

Note: The blocked list belongs to your account, never to the phone. Sign in on a second phone and the same people stay hidden. If somebody else signs in on your phone, they do not see your list and cannot undo your blocks. The Get help page says what the blocked person is told: "Blocking is silent: they are not told."

Undoing a block

1. Tap Profile at the bottom of the screen.
2. Scroll down and tap Blocked people.
3. Tap Unblock beside the name.
4. Tap Unblock again in the question to go ahead.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (3)
text:
The question at step four names the person, so it reads "Unblock Helen?", with the line "Their profile, requests, and messages can appear for you again." underneath. Keep blocked leaves things as they are. When it works, Towinly says the person's name and "can appear again." If it cannot reach Towinly it says "Could not unblock right now. Please try again." and the block stands.

Note: There is a second way, and it behaves differently. If you open a blocked person's page, the Unblock button on it asks no question at all. One tap undoes the block, and Towinly says "Unblocked." The same failure sentence appears if it cannot reach Towinly.

Unblocking removes the hiding and nothing more. A friendship that ended when you blocked them stays ended. To be friends again, one of you sends a fresh request. If the blocked list itself will not load you see "We couldn't load your blocked list right now. Please check your connection and try again." with a Try again button, and that message stands in place of the list, so a dropped connection can never look like an empty list.

The Blocked people screen with nobody blocked yet.

Reporting somebody

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (4)
text:
Report this person asks "What went wrong?" and offers the same four answers in the same order every time: Unsafe behavior, Harassment, Scam or fraud, Something else. Never mind closes it and sends nothing. On an iPhone the four answers rise from the bottom of the screen and the list closes the moment you tap one. On an Android phone and in a web browser the four answers open inside the page instead, the answer you tapped reads "Sending…" while it goes, and the other three cannot be tapped until it finishes.

When it works you see "Report sent. Thank you for keeping Towinly safe." If it fails: "Could not send the report. Please try again." If you have not confirmed your email address yet, Towinly says "Please verify your email first. Check your inbox for the link, then try again." Reporting does not hide the person. Block them as well if you want them out of your app.

Ending a friendship

1. Open the person's page.
2. Tap End friendship at the foot of the page.
3. Tap End it in the question to go ahead.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (5)
text:
The question reads "End this friendship?", with the line "You and Helen will no longer be connected. This cannot be undone." underneath, naming your friend. Keep friendship stops there. When it works Towinly says "Friendship ended." and the page then offers Add as friend again, so a fresh start is possible later. If it fails you see "Could not do that right now. Please try again." and you are still friends.

Taking a break

If a friendship is only wearing on you, a break is gentler than ending it. Take a break sits on the home screen. An elder finds it under My Helpers, a helper under My Elders. Tap the person's name to open their row, and Take a break sits at the bottom of what opens. Tapping their picture opens their page, which is a different screen and carries no break button.

The question is "Take a break?" on both sides, and the buttons are Not now and Take a break. The line underneath differs by seat. An elder reads "Trust steps and messages with Ethan pause until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost.", naming the helper. A helper reads "Trust steps and messages with this elder pause until either of you resumes. Nothing is lost.", with no name in it.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (6)
text:
Tip: After a break starts, Towinly says "Paused. You can resume any time." and puts an Undo button in that message for about six seconds. The friendship stays on your home screen as a card reading "On a break. Trust steps and messages are paused." with a Resume button, in the same list it was in before. Tapping Resume gives back "Welcome back. Trust steps and messages are on again." If the pause itself fails you see "Could not pause right now. Please try again."

Emergency contacts

The Emergency contacts screen: the line at the top, My contacts with one saved contact, then the three boxes under Add a contact.

1. Tap Profile at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap Emergency contacts, the last row in the group that begins with Trust Score.
3. Under Add a contact, type their name in Name.
4. Type their number in Phone number.
5. Type who they are in Who they are to you.
6. Tap Add contact.

The hint under the third box reads: Like "daughter", "neighbor", or "family friend". You may leave that box empty, and Towinly then saves the word Contact in its place. The keyboard walks the three boxes for you: next moves from Name to Phone number to Who they are to you, and done adds the contact.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (7)
text:
Each saved person is one row: their name, then who they are to you and their number under it. Tapping the row opens your phone app with the number ready. If your phone has no phone app, Towinly says "Could not open the phone app." and follows it with that person's name and number to dial by hand. There is no way to correct a contact once saved. To fix a wrong digit, remove the contact and add it again.

The red bin at the right of a row removes that contact at once, with no question first. Towinly says the person's name and "removed.", and puts an Undo button in that message for about six seconds. Undo puts the contact back with the same name, number and description. Wait longer than that and you type it in again. If the removal fails you see "Could not remove the contact. Please try again.", and the contact stays.

The two text messages Towinly sends by itself

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (8)
text:
The first goes out when an elder and a helper both agree to the sixth of the seven trust steps, Met in person. Every emergency contact on that elder's list gets it. It reads: "Your contact has arranged their first in-person meeting (connection: " then a long code, then "). Stay alert." The code in round brackets is how Towinly tells one friendship from another. There is no address and no time in it, and no names. A family member arranging a meeting with a helper for themselves does not set it off.

The second goes out when an elder has not used Towinly for five days. Towinly checks once a day and then texts every emergency contact on that elder's list: "Your contact on Towinly has not been active for 5 days. Please check in on them." It will not send that again for another seven days. Both texts follow an elder's account. A helper may save emergency contacts and call them, and neither text is sent for a helper.

Note: If the elder has family linked in Towinly, both events also leave a note inside the app for that family. The first-meeting note is written only when the elder has chosen to share that friendship with family.

heading: For everybody / Staying safe (9)
text: Take care: There is no SOS button in Towinly. Nothing on any screen calls the emergency services for you. Tapping a name on Emergency contacts opens your phone app with that number ready, and you make the call yourself. The two texts above are the only text messages Towinly sends by itself. In an emergency, call your local emergency number first, then call the people on this list.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (1)
text:
A copy of everything, or the end of everything. Both live in the same place.

At the bottom of Profile, above Log out, is a row called Account and data. Tap it to open two buttons.

A copy of your data

Account and data is one row near the bottom of Profile, just above Log out, and it is in the same place whether you are here as an elder, as a helper, or for a family member. It stays folded shut until you tap it, so that Delete my account is never sitting in the open where a wrong tap can reach it. Tapping the row unfolds two lines of words: Send me a copy of my data in blue, and Delete my account in red. Tapping the row again folds them away.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (2)
text:
Take care: On a phone the copy is handed over as writing, not as a file with that name on it. The name Towinly - my information.txt is used as the subject if you send it to yourself by mail, so do not go hunting for a file by that name on your phone. On an iPhone, closing the sharing screen without choosing anywhere keeps nothing, and Towinly says nothing either. On an Android phone Towinly cannot tell whether you kept it, so it says Your copy is ready. Choose where to keep it. whatever you did. Open the place you saved to and look at the copy with your own eyes before you delete anything.

The copy is plain writing, so it opens on any machine, in any year, with nothing installed. The first line is Your Towinly information. The second line begins Made on and gives the day. Then comes this: "This is everything Towinly holds about you on the day it was made. Keep it somewhere safe. Towinly does not keep a copy of this file for you." After that it is laid out under headings in ordinary words.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (3)
text:
The copy lists what is in your Sealed box: what sort of thing each one is, how big it is, and when you put it there. It does not contain what is inside them. The file says so in that very place: "What is inside these is not in this file. Towinly locks your Sealed box with your password and cannot read it, so it cannot copy it out for you. To keep what is inside, open your Sealed box and save each thing yourself."

Deleting your account

Nothing is removed until you answer the second question. Tapping the dimmed part of the screen outside either question is the same as stopping. While it works the words read Deleting…. When it is done Towinly says Your account has been deleted. and signs you out. If something goes wrong it says Could not delete the account right now. Please try again. and your account is still there.

It happens at the moment you answer that second question. There is no waiting period and nothing is held back in case you change your mind. Towinly's own page on the web names one exception, in these words: "Backups are the one exception: we have not fixed how long a copy can sit in one of those, and we will write the number here when we have."

What deleting removes

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (4)
text:
Two things do not go with you. A story another member wrote that mentions you is their words, and it stays. A letter another member wrote and addressed to you stays as well, for the same reason: it belongs to whoever wrote it, and closing your account does not close theirs. That letter is no longer addressed to anybody after your account goes, so it can never be delivered.

Take care: Your Keyholders are not told, and there is nothing left to be passed on afterwards. If you were holding a key for somebody else, that ends too, so it is kind to tell them yourself first. Take your copy before you delete, and save anything out of your Sealed box by hand, because after the second question none of it can be brought back.

If you cannot get into the app

There is a page on the web for exactly this, at towinly.com/app/delete-account, and you do not need the app or a password to use it. It is written under seven headings.

- If you have the Towinly app
- If you do not have the app
- Take a copy first if you want one
- What your copy cannot include
- What deleting removes
- How soon it happens
- What stays

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (5)
text:
The one button on the page, Write to us and ask, starts a message to help@towinly.com with the subject Please delete my Towinly account. The message has three lines to fill in: the email address you joined with, the name on your profile, and whether you want a copy of your information first. Send it from the email address you joined with, so we can find your account and be sure it is you. The page also prints Or write to help@towinly.com yourself. underneath, so you can write by hand if no mail app opens.

A person here reads every one of these and does the deletion by hand, and writes back within seven days. If you have not heard back by then, write again and say it is your second time asking.

Privacy and terms

Privacy policy and Terms of service are two rows in Profile, written in plain words. Both open with the same honest heading, Draft: a lawyer has not checked this yet, a note saying Towinly wrote them itself from what the app actually does, and the day the draft was written, Draft of 16 August 2026.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (6)
text:
They are the same words you agreed to when you joined. On the create account screen you tick I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, and Read the Terms and Privacy Policy just below it opens both of them in one sheet. So the document you agreed to and the document you look up two years later cannot drift apart.

On where your information sits, the policy says it is kept on servers in the United States. Photos and identity documents are kept in Amazon S3, also in the United States.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (7)
text:
It then names every outside company that touches any of it, and what each one sees. Amazon keeps your photos and identity documents. Twilio sends the text messages, so it sees the phone number a message is going to. OpenStreetMap turns the name of your town into a rough position, and is told nothing about you. OpenAI writes the answers from the Towinly helper, and only when you have said yes to that. Railway runs the servers everything sits on. Expo delivers the notification that makes your phone ring, and sees the address your phone made for that purpose and the few words on the ping itself, such as a name. It never sees what a message says. None of them are allowed to sell your information or use it for their own purposes.

On safety, the policy says what you send is protected on its way to Towinly. Once it arrives, most of your information is stored without a second lock on it. The Sealed box is the exception: whatever you keep there is scrambled while it is stored, and the key that unscrambles it is not kept beside it.

heading: For everybody / Your data, and closing your account (8)
text:
The terms add one line worth remembering: nothing you write on Towinly is a will. No letter, note or story here can decide who inherits anything, and none of it replaces a will.

Near the end of the privacy policy, under Asking for a copy of your information, there is an underlined line you can tap, Delete your account on the web. It opens the page above in your browser.

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (1)
text:
Somebody at Towinly reads every message.

The Get help page. It opens without signing in. The Write to us button sits further down, past the six parts.

Open Profile, then Get help. The page explains what to do about the usual difficulties: finding your way around, helping an older parent, feeling unsafe about somebody, and closing your account. At the bottom, Write to us opens your email app with the address already filled in.

Towinly is small and new, so replies come from a person rather than a call centre.

What the Get help page says, part by part

Open Profile at the bottom of the screen, then tap Get help. The page starts with one short paragraph: Towinly connects older people with younger helpers for company and everyday help, and if something is not working, or you are unsure about someone you have met here, write to us. A person reads every message. Below that come six short parts, one under the other.

Asking to be linked to a parent, if you are the family member

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (2)
text:
The words on the Get help page name one button. Here is what a family member sees in the app. If no parent is linked yet, your Home screen shows a card headed No parent linked yet with a Add your parent button inside it. Once a parent is linked that card is gone, and the standing control is Add parent at the top of Home, next to the Towinly name.

The form asks for one thing first: "Type their exact Towinly username, email or phone. They must say yes before you see anything." A real name is not enough. If you leave the box empty the form says "Please enter a username, email, or phone number" and sends nothing.

The Write to us button, and what it opens

1. Tap Profile at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap Get help.
3. Read past the six parts to the blue Write to us button.
4. Tap Write to us. Your email app opens with the address help@towinly.com already filled in and the subject already written, "I need help with Towinly".
5. Type what you were doing and what happened, then send it in your email app. Towinly cannot send it for you.

That line sits under a thin rule, between the plain address and the Delete your account on the web link, so the deletion link is still below it.

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (3)
text:
Tip: Under the button the address sits in plain words: "Or write to help@towinly.com yourself." You can press and hold it to select and copy it, and write from any email you like.

Telling them what could be better

The feedback form: three boxes, then the star rows under Rate the app (optional), with Submit Feedback held at the bottom of the screen.

What the form asks | Do you have to fill it in
Name | No
Email | No
Message | Yes

Under the message box a small line says "Be honest! Include at least one thing you didn't like." Below the box, under the heading Rate the app (optional), sit seven rows you can rate from one star to five: Idea, How it looks, Theme, Feeling safe, Ease of Use, How fast it feels and Overall. Tap a star to set that row. Tap the same star again to clear the row back to nothing. Leaving every row blank is allowed.

1. Type what you want to say in Message.
2. Add your name and email if you want the team to know who wrote. Leave them empty if you would rather not say.
3. Rate any of the seven rows, or none of them.
4. Tap Submit Feedback at the bottom. It reads Sending… while it goes.

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (4)
text:
Take care: Nobody writes back to this form. What you send is saved for the Towinly team to read, and no message comes to your email. If you need an answer, use Write to us on the Get help page instead.

If the message box is empty, nothing is sent. The outline of the box turns red and a red line appears below it beside a warning circle: "Please write a message before submitting." It stands where the "Be honest!" line was. Typing in the box clears it away. If you typed something in Email that is not a full email address, nothing is sent either, and a short message about the address appears near the bottom of the screen for a few seconds.

When it does send, a short message says "Thank you. Your feedback helps Towinly grow." and the form closes, putting you back where you came from. If it cannot reach Towinly, a message says "Could not send it right now. Please try again." and everything you typed stays on screen, so you lose nothing.

Reporting an answer the Towinly helper gave

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (5)
text:
The Ask AI button floats above the bottom bar on the tab screens, with one exception: it is not there on the screen the raised middle button opens, which is Ask Help for an elder and Offer Help for a helper. What the helper writes is written by a machine, so it can be wrong.

The helper on opening: the greeting, its own Read aloud, and three questions you can tap. Report this answer belongs under an answer, so it is not here yet.

1. Tap Report this answer under the answer that worried you.
2. The helper closes and the feedback form opens by itself.
3. The message box is already filled in for you. It says you want to report an answer from the Towinly helper, quotes the answer word for word, and leaves "What was wrong with it:" waiting at the end.
4. Type what was wrong under that line.
5. Tap Submit Feedback.

The question asked before your first question

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (6)
text:
The first question you ever ask on your account stops for a plain question titled "Before your first question". It names OpenAI, the outside AI service that writes the answers, and says your question, this chat, and a short summary of your own Towinly activity are shared with OpenAI. It gives your first name and trust score as examples of that summary. It also says your contact details are never shared, and that the answers are written by a machine and can be wrong.

Take care: The summary is wider than the two examples. Along with your first name and trust score it can carry which seat you use, your city, whether your identity is verified, your daily streak and your best one, whether you checked in today, how many people you are connected to, how many requests are waiting on your reply, how many help requests you have open, and any part of your profile you have not finished. Your email, phone and messages are not among them.

heading: For everybody / Getting help from a person (7)
text:
Answer Yes, that's okay and your question goes at once, and the box empties. Answer Not now and nothing is sent, and your words stay where you typed them. If you tapped one of the three suggested questions instead of typing, there was nothing in the box either way.

Note: You are asked once for each account, not once for each phone. If somebody else signs in on the same phone, the question comes back for them on their own first question.

If Towinly is reached but the AI service cannot answer, a different sentence comes back: "Sorry, I can't answer just now. Please try again in a moment. If it keeps happening, use the Feedback button and the Towinly team will help." There is no button called Feedback anywhere in the app. The row it means is Share feedback on your Profile page.
